conflicts.description: Differences in attribute and entity naming across schemas: bank2 uses branch_name/branch_address while bank1 uses name/address; bank1 uses custid/name/phone while bank2 uses customer_id/customer_name/mobileno; bank1 uses account_no/acc_type/balance while bank2 uses account_id/account_type/account_balance; bridge tables availed_by in bank1 corresponds to borrower in bank2; hold_by in bank1 corresponds to customer-account relationship.
conflicts.resolution: Adopted normalized, standardized snake_case naming conventions (e.g., customer, account, branch, loan, loan_customer, customer_account).

conflicts.description: Loan amount representation: bank1 defines a single 'amount' while bank2 distinguishes 'issued_amount' and 'remaining_amount'.
conflicts.resolution: Retained 'amount' / 'issued_amount' as total issued amount and included 'remaining_amount' as an optional field in loan.

conflicts.description: Account balance and loan amount are defined as 'number' (floating-point) in bank1 but 'integer' in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized financial amounts and balances to 'number' in the target schema to accommodate fractional currency units without loss of precision.

conflicts.description: bank1 contains bank institutional information (bank table with code, name, address) whereas bank2 models branches directly without a parent bank entity.
conflicts.resolution: Maintained bank as a parent resource with bank_code foreign keys on branch where applicable.

conflicts.description: bank2 contains entities not present in bank1: banker_info, customer_credit_card, and loan_payment.
conflicts.resolution: Included banker_info, credit_card, and loan_payment as distinct first-class resources in the target schema.

conflicts.description: Redundant relationship tables in bank1: bank1 defines 'offer' (branch-loan) and 'maintain' (branch-account) while both loan and account already possess direct foreign keys to branch.
conflicts.resolution: Omitted redundant relationship tables offer and maintain in favor of direct branch_id foreign keys present on account and loan in both schemas.

conflicts.description: Customer-to-account relationship: bank1 supports an N:M relationship via bridge table 'hold_by', whereas bank2 models customer with a single foreign key 'account_id' (implying N:1 or 1:1) and credit cards/transactions also linking customer and account.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized customer-to-account relationships into an N:M junction table 'customer_account' (incorporating bank1.hold_by and bank2's customer-account relationship) to accommodate multi-account ownership and joint accounts.

conflicts.description: Customer-to-loan relationship: bank1 models N:M via availed_by (composite PK [custid, loan_id]) while bank2 models N:M via borrower with a surrogate PK borrower_id.
conflicts.resolution: Unified loan borrower / availed_by relationship into a single associative entity 'loan_borrower' with composite key [customer_id, loan_id].

conflicts.description: bank2.borrower uses a surrogate primary key (borrower_id) whereas bank1.availed_by uses a composite primary key (custid, loan_id).
conflicts.resolution: Defined composite primary key [customer_id, loan_id] for the unified loan_borrower bridge table; mapped source identifiers accordingly.

conflicts.description: Synonymous naming for customer identification, customer name, and customer contact number across bank1 and bank2 (e.g., custid vs customer_id, name vs customer_name, phone vs mobileno).
conflicts.resolution: Standardized customer table columns to snake_case canonical names: customer_id, customer_name, and phone_number.

conflicts.description: Synonymous naming for branch attributes between bank1 and bank2 (e.g., name vs branch_name, address vs branch_address).
conflicts.resolution: Standardized branch table columns to canonical names: branch_id, branch_name, and address.

conflicts.description: Synonymous naming for account attributes between bank1 and bank2 (e.g., account_no vs account_id, acc_type vs account_type, balance vs account_balance).
conflicts.resolution: Standardized account table attributes to account_id, account_type, and balance.

conflicts.description: Synonymous naming between bank1 availed_by association and bank2 borrower table.
conflicts.resolution: Adopted loan_customer (or loan_borrower) associative table naming to consistently capture customer-loan relationships.

conflicts.description: Data type representation difference for monetary values: bank1 uses floating number for balances/amounts whereas bank2 uses integer.
conflicts.resolution: Unified monetary fields (account balance, loan amounts, transaction amounts) under the number type to support decimal precision.

conflicts.description: bank1 models bank institution in an explicit parent entity 'bank' with 'branch' referencing 'bank', whereas bank2 lacks a dedicated bank entity.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved the normalized 'bank' entity and made bank_code optional on branch to accommodate bank2 branches where bank parent is undefined.

conflicts.description: bank1 models many-to-many relationships using dedicated bridge tables (offer, maintain, availed_by, hold_by) alongside direct foreign keys, while bank2 uses direct foreign keys and separate relationship tables (borrower). Specifically, customer-account is M:N in bank1 (hold_by) but 1:N / directly referenced in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved the M:N associative bridge table customer_account (merging hold_by and bank2 customer-account association) and loan_customer (merging availed_by and borrower), while maintaining foreign keys to branches on loan and account.

conflicts.description: bank2 includes specialized operational entities (banker_info, transaction, customer_credit_card, loan_payment) not present in bank1.
conflicts.resolution: Retained banker_info, transaction, customer_credit_card, and loan_payment as first-class resources in the global schema to preserve operational granularity.

conflicts.description: Customer to Account relationship cardinality mismatch: bank1 allows an M:N relationship via hold_by, whereas bank2 establishes a direct 1:N or 1:1 foreign key customer.account_id.
conflicts.resolution: Resolved in favor of the more general M:N relationship using the customer_account association table, removing the restrictive single account_id foreign key from customer.

conflicts.description: bank1 availed_by uses a composite primary key (Custid, Loan_id) whereas bank2 borrower uses a surrogate primary key borrower_id.
conflicts.resolution: Used the natural composite primary key [customer_id, loan_id] for the unified customer_loan table to ensure uniqueness without redundant surrogate keys.

conflicts.description: Loan amount semantics: bank1 specifies a single loan amount, whereas bank2 distinguishes between issued_amount and remaining_amount.
conflicts.resolution: Mapped bank1.loan.amount to amount (total/issued amount) and maintained remaining_amount as a distinct optional attribute for current debt tracking.

conflicts.description: Entity and attribute name variations across bank1 and bank2: branch name ('name' vs 'branch_name'), address ('address' vs 'branch_address'), customer identifiers ('custid' vs 'customer_id'), customer names ('name' vs 'customer_name'), phone numbers ('phone' vs 'mobileno'), account identifiers ('account_no' vs 'account_id'), and account types ('acc_type' vs 'account_type').
conflicts.resolution: Standardized table and attribute names using descriptive snake_case naming conventions (e.g., branch_name, customer_id, account_id, account_type, phone_number).

conflicts.description: Customer-loan association table naming: bank1 names the association 'availed_by' while bank2 names it 'borrower'.
conflicts.resolution: Consolidated into the standard associative entity 'loan_borrower' (or 'borrower').

conflicts.description: Monetary amount and balance attributes use number (float/decimal) in bank1 but integer in bank2 (e.g., account balance, loan amount).
conflicts.resolution: Standardized all monetary amounts and balance fields to generic type 'number' to accommodate fractional currency units without loss of precision.

conflicts.description: In bank1, 'loan.amount' represents the total principal loan amount, whereas in bank2, loans explicitly distinguish between 'issued_amount' and 'remaining_amount'.
conflicts.resolution: Mapped bank1.loan.amount and bank2.loan.issued_amount to target field 'amount' (principal/issued amount), and retained 'remaining_amount' as an optional field for schemas providing balance tracking.

conflicts.description: bank1 models an enterprise hierarchy starting with a 'bank' entity with multiple branches, whereas bank2 only models standalone branches without a parent bank entity.
conflicts.resolution: Retained 'bank' as an independent parent resource, making the 'bank_code' reference in 'branch' optional so branches without a parent bank (such as in bank2) can be accommodated.

conflicts.description: bank2 includes domain-specific entities not present in bank1: banker information ('banker_info'), customer credit cards ('customer_credit_card'), and loan payment history ('loan_payment'). Additionally, bank1 contains explicit M:N or redundant bridge tables ('offer', 'maintain') which duplicate direct foreign key relationships.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved banker_info, customer_credit_card, and loan_payment in the target schema. Retained direct foreign keys for account-branch and loan-branch relationships, while deprecating redundant binary relationship tables where direct FKs suffice.

conflicts.description: Customer-to-account relationship: bank1 models a many-to-many relationship via 'hold_by', whereas bank2 embeds a single 'account_id' foreign key directly inside the 'customer' table (1:N or N:1 constraint).
conflicts.resolution: Adopted a normalized bridge resource 'customer_account' (derived from bank1.hold_by and bank2's customer-account relationship) to support many-to-many account ownership without loss of generality.

conflicts.description: Bridge table primary keys: bank1.availed_by uses composite key (custid, loan_id), whereas bank2.borrower defines a surrogate primary key (borrower_id).
conflicts.resolution: Used composite primary key (customer_id, loan_id) for the associative table 'loan_borrower' to ensure relational uniqueness across customer-loan pairs.

conflicts.description: The same customer identifier uses abbreviated and descriptive names.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized the identifier as customer_id.

conflicts.description: The account identity is named as an account number in one schema and an account ID in the other.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized the unified account identity as account_id while preserving both source primary-key provenances.

conflicts.description: Equivalent account attributes use abbreviated versus expanded names.
conflicts.resolution: Adopted the explicit snake_case names account_type and balance_amount.

conflicts.description: Generic branch attribute names in bank1 are entity-qualified in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized them as branch_name and address_text.

conflicts.description: Customer telephone number uses different labels.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized it as phone_number.

conflicts.description: The customer-loan relationship is named as availed_by in one schema and borrower in the other.
conflicts.resolution: Represented the common relationship in a borrower resource.

conflicts.description: The original loan amount is generically named in bank1 and explicitly named in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized the attribute as issued_amount.

conflicts.description: Account balance is number in bank1 but integer in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Used number to retain fractional monetary values without loss.

conflicts.description: Loan amount is number in bank1 but integer in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Used number as the lossless common generic type.

conflicts.description: Monetary quantities are encoded as integers even though fractional currency values may occur.
conflicts.resolution: Used number for monetary amount fields in the target schema.

conflicts.description: Bank1 supplies one generic loan amount, whereas bank2 distinguishes issued and remaining amounts.
conflicts.resolution: Interpreted bank1 amount as the original/issued principal and kept remaining_amount as a separate attribute; the interpretation is documented rather than conflating the two measures.

conflicts.description: The schemas omit currency codes and monetary scale conventions.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved values as generic numeric monetary amounts and explicitly documented that currency is unspecified; no unsupported currency conversion was inferred.

conflicts.description: Bank1 contains both a branch directly recorded on an account and a separate branch-maintains-account relationship, which may represent home ownership versus operational maintenance.
conflicts.resolution: Kept home_branch_id on account and account_maintenance as a distinct relationship instead of merging potentially different meanings.

conflicts.description: Bank1 separately records a branch on a loan and branches that offer a loan, which are not necessarily the same relationship.
conflicts.resolution: Kept originating_branch_id on loan and represented offerings separately in branch_loan_offer.

conflicts.description: Bank1 models banks and branch-to-bank membership, while bank2 starts at the branch level and has no bank entity.
conflicts.resolution: Retained a bank resource and an optional branch.bank_code relationship so bank2 branches can exist without fabricated bank records.

conflicts.description: Bank1 normalizes customer-account holdings into a bridge, while bank2 embeds an account foreign key in customer.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized both representations into the customer_account bridge.

conflicts.description: Bank1 uses a composite-key association table, while bank2 uses a borrower entity with a surrogate key.
conflicts.resolution: Unified the relationship as a composite-key borrower resource and retained bank2's source-specific borrower identifier as a non-key attribute.

conflicts.description: Branch-loan association is represented both as a separate offering table and as a direct loan foreign key.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved the semantically distinct offering bridge and the direct originating-branch relationship.

conflicts.description: Branch-account association is separately decomposed as maintenance in bank1 but also embedded directly on account in both schemas.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved account_maintenance separately while standardizing the direct account branch as home_branch_id.

conflicts.description: Bank2 contains operational entities that have no counterparts in bank1.
conflicts.resolution: Retained them as normalized target resources linked through foreign keys.

conflicts.description: Bank1 permits a many-to-many customer-account relationship, while bank2 records one account per customer row.
conflicts.resolution: Used the more general many-to-many customer_account bridge, which can represent bank2's narrower case.

conflicts.description: Bank1 permits multiple branches to offer a loan while both schemas can also associate a loan directly with one branch.
conflicts.resolution: Modeled offering as many-to-many and retained the optional single originating branch independently.

conflicts.description: Bank1 permits many-to-many maintenance while direct account fields imply at most one primary branch.
conflicts.resolution: Represented maintenance as many-to-many and home branch as an optional many-accounts-to-one-branch relationship.

conflicts.description: Both sources support customer-loan associations, but bank2 assigns a separate row identity and may allow duplicate customer-loan pairs unless constrained outside the schema.
conflicts.resolution: Used one canonical borrower relationship per customer-loan pair through a composite primary key.

conflicts.description: Equivalent account entities use differently named primary keys.
conflicts.resolution: Unified both as the account.account_id primary key.

conflicts.description: Equivalent customer entities use differently named primary keys.
conflicts.resolution: Unified both as the customer.customer_id primary key.

conflicts.description: Bank1 declares mixed-case composite primary-key names that do not match its lowercase fields, while bank2 uses a surrogate borrower key.
conflicts.resolution: Used the valid lowercase semantic pair customer_id and loan_id as the target composite key and retained borrower_id separately.

conflicts.description: Several bank1 composite keys and foreign keys use case variants that do not correspond to declared field names.
conflicts.resolution: Canonicalized all key fields to the actual lowercase snake_case target fields and declared each foreign key once.

conflicts.description: The sources contain duplicate foreign-key declarations, and bank1 additionally includes case-invalid duplicate references.
conflicts.resolution: Removed duplicate declarations and retained one valid target foreign key per relationship.

conflicts.description: Primary-key values originate in separate source systems and may occupy overlapping numeric namespaces.
conflicts.resolution: Aligned them as common business identifiers in the global schema; operational integration must ensure identity reconciliation before co-loading, without conflating this conceptual schema with execution rules.

conflicts.description: The customer-loan relationship is named availed_by in bank1 and borrower in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Named the normalized relationship resource loan_borrower.

conflicts.description: The source table name includes an informational suffix rather than naming the entity directly.
conflicts.resolution: Renamed the target entity resource to banker.

conflicts.description: The source table embeds ownership context in the credit-card entity name.
conflicts.resolution: Named the target entity credit_card and represented ownership with a customer_id foreign key.

conflicts.description: Account balance is number in bank1 but integer in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Used number to preserve fractional monetary values and safely accommodate both representations.

conflicts.description: Loan principal is number in bank1 but integer in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Used number for the unified issued_amount.

conflicts.description: Monetary quantities are encoded as integers, which may prevent representation of fractional currency amounts.
conflicts.resolution: Used the generic number type for monetary measures in the target.

conflicts.description: bank1 supplies one undifferentiated loan amount, while bank2 distinguishes issued principal from the remaining balance.
conflicts.resolution: Interpreted bank1 amount as original principal and unified it with issued_amount; retained remaining_amount as a separate attribute to avoid conflating principal and outstanding balance.

conflicts.description: The schemas contain monetary values without currency codes or declared minor-unit scales.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved values as number fields with amount-qualified names and documented that currency is unspecified; no unsupported currency conversion was inferred.

conflicts.description: Addresses are supplied as opaque strings, so their internal component semantics cannot be reliably aligned or split.
conflicts.resolution: Retained each address as an atomic source-supplied string rather than inventing unverified street, locality, or postal-code components.

conflicts.description: Customer-account ownership is modeled as a separate association table in bank1 but embedded as an account foreign key on customer in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized ownership into the customer_account relationship resource.

conflicts.description: Account-branch maintenance is represented both as a relationship table and as embedded foreign keys.
conflicts.resolution: Centralized the relationship in account_branch and removed branch_id from the account entity.

conflicts.description: Loan-branch association is represented both as an offer table and as embedded branch foreign keys.
conflicts.resolution: Centralized the relationship in loan_branch and removed branch_id from the loan entity.

conflicts.description: One schema uses a pure bridge while the other uses a relationship entity with its own identifier.
conflicts.resolution: Used a normalized loan_borrower bridge and retained bank2's relationship identifier as a source-specific non-key attribute.

conflicts.description: bank1 explicitly models banks and their branches, whereas bank2 begins at the branch level and has no bank entity or bank reference.
conflicts.resolution: Retained bank as an optional higher-level entity and made branch.bank_code nullable for sources without bank-level data.

conflicts.description: bank1 permits many-to-many customer-account holdings, while bank2 records one account reference per customer row.
conflicts.resolution: Used a many-to-many customer_account bridge, which preserves bank1 joint holdings and represents bank2's narrower relationship without loss.

conflicts.description: The maintain bridge can express multiple branches per account, while embedded branch_id columns imply one branch per account.
conflicts.resolution: Used account_branch with a composite key to support the more general many-to-many cardinality.

conflicts.description: The offer bridge can associate a loan with multiple branches, while direct branch_id columns imply one branch per loan.
conflicts.resolution: Used loan_branch with a composite key to preserve the more general relationship.

conflicts.description: Both sources permit customer-loan associations, but bank2 can technically contain multiple borrower rows for the same customer and loan because borrower_id is its key.
conflicts.resolution: Defined one canonical customer-loan association per composite pair and retained the source borrower identifier for lineage.

conflicts.description: Several bank1 primary-key declarations use capitalization that does not match the actual lowercase field names.
conflicts.resolution: Defined valid lowercase composite keys using the actual normalized relationship fields.

conflicts.description: bank1 contains duplicate foreign-key declarations, including case-variant references to fields that do not exist with the declared capitalization.
conflicts.resolution: Removed duplicate and invalid case-variant declarations and retained one valid foreign key per relationship.

conflicts.description: bank2 repeats each listed foreign-key declaration.
conflicts.resolution: Deduplicated foreign keys in the unified schema.

conflicts.description: bank1 keys the borrower relationship by customer and loan, while bank2 uses a surrogate borrower_id.
conflicts.resolution: Used the semantically meaningful composite customer_id and loan_id as the global key and retained borrower_id separately for source traceability.

conflicts.description: Equivalent account entities use differently named primary keys.
conflicts.resolution: Unified them under account_id with both source primary keys recorded in provenance.

conflicts.description: Equivalent customer entities use differently named primary keys.
conflicts.resolution: Unified them under customer_id with both source primary keys recorded in provenance.

conflicts.description: Equivalent account identifiers and attributes use abbreviated, numbered, and descriptive names.
conflicts.resolution: Adopted the canonical snake_case names account_id, account_type, and balance_amount.

conflicts.description: Equivalent customer identifiers, names, and phone numbers use different labels.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized them as customer_id, customer_name, and phone_number.

conflicts.description: Branch attributes use generic names in one source and entity-qualified names in the other.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized them as branch_name and postal_address.

conflicts.description: The original loan amount is generically named in bank1 and explicitly named in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Used issued_amount to distinguish original principal from remaining_amount.

conflicts.description: Declared keys and references use inconsistent capitalization and names that do not match the actual lowercase fields.
conflicts.resolution: Canonicalized all target names to lowercase snake_case and based target constraints on the actual declared fields.

conflicts.description: Some source resource names are verbose or overly generic.
conflicts.resolution: Used the concise entity names banker and credit_card, and the context-specific name account_transaction.

conflicts.description: Account balance is number in bank1 but integer in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Used number to preserve fractional monetary values without losing integer values.

conflicts.description: Loan principal is number in bank1 but integer in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Used number as the common, non-lossy generic type.

conflicts.description: Monetary quantities are represented as integers, which may preclude fractional values.
conflicts.resolution: Used number for monetary measures in the target while retaining date and identifier types unchanged.

conflicts.description: Bank1 has one generic loan amount while bank2 distinguishes issued and remaining amounts.
conflicts.resolution: Interpreted bank1 amount as original principal, unified it with issued_amount, and retained remaining_amount separately.

conflicts.description: A direct account-to-branch assignment is semantically distinct from bank1's explicit maintenance relationship.
conflicts.resolution: Retained direct branch assignment on account and modeled maintenance as a separate relationship resource.

conflicts.description: A loan's directly assigned branch is semantically distinct from the set of branches that offer a loan.
conflicts.resolution: Retained branch_id on loan and preserved offering relationships in branch_loan_offer.

conflicts.description: Address values may be internally composite, but neither source defines component structure.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved each as an opaque postal_address string rather than inventing unsubstantiated address components.

conflicts.description: The sources do not provide currency codes or units for monetary values.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved monetary values in their source monetary unit and avoided unsupported currency conversion or SI-unit claims.

conflicts.description: Customer-account association is a bridge table in bank1 but embedded as an account foreign key in bank2 customer.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized both representations into customer_account and removed the relationship attribute from the unified customer entity.

conflicts.description: The customer-loan association is represented by a composite bridge in bank1 and an identified associative entity in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Unified both as customer_loan while preserving bank2's association identifier as the target association key.

conflicts.description: Bank1 contains both an offering bridge and a direct loan branch reference, whereas bank2 contains only a direct reference.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved the semantically distinct direct assignment and offering structures.

conflicts.description: Bank1 contains both a maintenance bridge and a direct account branch reference, whereas bank2 contains only a direct reference.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved the semantically distinct direct assignment and maintenance structures.

conflicts.description: Bank1 models banks above branches, while bank2 has branches without a bank entity or bank reference.
conflicts.resolution: Retained bank as an optional parent of branch so bank2 branches can coexist without fabricated bank records.

conflicts.description: Bank1 supports a many-to-many customer-account relationship, while bank2 assigns exactly one account to each customer.
conflicts.resolution: Used the more general many-to-many customer_account bridge; bank2 rows form a constrained subset of it.

conflicts.description: Both sources support repeated customer-loan associations structurally, but bank1 enforces uniqueness by customer-loan pair while bank2 uses a separate borrower identifier.
conflicts.resolution: Modeled customer-loan participation as an associative resource capable of preserving bank2 association identities.

conflicts.description: The offering bridge permits multiple branches per loan while direct branch columns permit at most one assigned branch per loan.
conflicts.resolution: Represented offering and direct assignment as separate relationships rather than collapsing their cardinalities.

conflicts.description: The maintenance bridge permits multiple branches per account while direct branch columns permit at most one assigned branch per account.
conflicts.resolution: Represented maintenance and direct assignment separately.

conflicts.description: The same account entity uses differently named primary keys.
conflicts.resolution: Unified them under account_id and retained both source primary-key provenances.

conflicts.description: The same customer entity uses differently named primary keys.
conflicts.resolution: Unified them under customer_id and retained both source primary-key provenances.

conflicts.description: Bank1 declares a composite association key with capitalization errors, whereas bank2 uses a surrogate borrower key.
conflicts.resolution: Used bank2's association identifier as customer_loan_id; generated values are required for bank1 associations, while customer_id and loan_id preserve their relationship identities.

conflicts.description: Several bank1 primary-key declarations reference nonexistent case variants rather than the actual lowercase fields.
conflicts.resolution: Defined valid target composite keys using canonical lowercase fields and made all primary-key components required.

conflicts.description: The sources contain invalid case-variant or duplicate foreign-key declarations.
conflicts.resolution: Removed duplicate and invalid declarations and retained one valid foreign key per conceptual relationship.

conflicts.description: Cardinality representation conflict: bank1 uses direct many-to-many table (availed_by) while bank2 uses borrower entity with surrogate key
conflicts.resolution: Standardized to natural key bridge table (customer_loan) to represent the many-to-many relationship

conflicts.description: Foreign key presence conflict: bank1 branches reference bank via bank_code while bank2 branches have no bank reference

conflicts.description: Primary key naming inconsistency across schemas for equivalent entities

conflicts.description: Customer name column uses the generic name 'name' in bank1 and 'customer_name' in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized to 'customer_name' to avoid ambiguity with other name columns.

conflicts.description: The customer telephone attribute is 'phone' in bank1 and 'mobileno' in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized to 'phone' as the canonical customer contact field.

conflicts.description: Branch name is 'name' in bank1 and 'branch_name' in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized to 'branch_name'.

conflicts.description: Branch address is 'address' in bank1 and 'branch_address' in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized to 'address' within the branch resource.

conflicts.description: Account primary key is 'account_no' in bank1 and 'account_id' in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized to 'account_id'.

conflicts.description: Account category attribute is abbreviated 'acc_type' in bank1 and 'account_type' in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized to 'account_type'.

conflicts.description: Account balance is 'balance' in bank1 and 'account_balance' in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized to 'balance' within the account resource.

conflicts.description: The loan principal is named generically 'amount' in bank1 and 'issued_amount' in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized to 'issued_amount' to disambiguate from other amount columns (transaction.amount, loan_payment.amount).

conflicts.description: bank1 contains inconsistent casing/homonyms for the same conceptual columns (e.g. 'branch_id' vs 'Branch_id', 'account_no' vs 'Account_No', 'loan_id' vs 'Loan_id', 'custid' vs 'Custid', 'bank_code' vs 'Bank_Code'). Several FK entries reference capitalized field names that do not exist as declared columns.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized all identifiers to lower snake_case, collapsing each casing variant to a single canonical column and dropping the dangling capitalized FK references.

conflicts.description: bank1 models an explicit 'bank' entity while bank2 has no bank concept; branch-level attributes overlap the naming of bank-level attributes.
conflicts.resolution: Retained a distinct 'bank' resource (bank1 only) and kept 'branch' as the shared branch resource, avoiding name collision.

conflicts.description: Monetary values are typed as 'number' in bank1 (account.balance, loan.amount) but as 'integer' in bank2 (account_balance, issued_amount, remaining_amount, assets, transaction.amount, loan_payment.amount, card_limit).
conflicts.resolution: Unified all monetary columns to the generic 'number' type to accommodate fractional currency amounts without loss of precision.

conflicts.description: Identifier columns are consistently integer in both schemas; no numeric/string mismatch, but bank1.bank.code (string) vs branch-level code semantics differ.
conflicts.resolution: Kept all surrogate entity identifiers as integer; retained bank_code as string since it is a business code, not a numeric surrogate.

conflicts.description: bank1 represents the loan with a single 'amount', whereas bank2 decomposes the loan into 'issued_amount' and 'remaining_amount', implying distinct monetary semantics for issued vs outstanding amounts.
conflicts.resolution: Mapped bank1.loan.amount to the issued principal ('issued_amount') and kept 'remaining_amount' as a separate bank2-only attribute, preserving both distinct semantics.

conflicts.description: Monetary balances/assets appear as integer counts in bank2 versus decimal 'number' in bank1, implying differing scale/precision conventions for the same financial quantities.
conflicts.resolution: Adopted a uniform fractional-capable representation ('number') for all monetary quantities and documented the semantic equivalence.

conflicts.description: The customer-account association is modeled as an explicit many-to-many relationship table (hold_by) in bank1 but as a single embedded 'account_id' FK on the customer row in bank2, conflating account ownership semantics.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized both into the 'customer_account' bridge resource; the bank2 embedded FK is treated as one instance of the M:N ownership relation.

conflicts.description: 'phone' (generic) and 'mobileno' (mobile-specific) may denote the same contact channel but with differing specificity.
conflicts.resolution: Treated both as the same customer telephone attribute 'phone'.

conflicts.description: bank1 distinguishes bank-level name/address from branch-level name/address; bank2 only has branch-level data, risking conflation of bank vs branch identity.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved bank-level attributes only in the 'bank' resource and branch-level attributes in 'branch', keeping the two identity scopes semantically separated.

conflicts.description: bank1 heavily normalizes relationships into dedicated associative tables (offer, maintain, availed_by, hold_by), while bank2 embeds some relationships inline and introduces additional entities (borrower, loan_payment, transaction, customer_credit_card, banker_info) absent from bank1.
conflicts.resolution: Retained bank2-only entities as standalone resources and re-expressed bank1's associative tables as bridge resources; overlapping relations (availed_by/borrower) were merged.

conflicts.description: bank2 embeds the account relationship directly on the customer table (denormalized 1:1 style), conflicting with bank1's normalized associative structures.
conflicts.resolution: Removed the embedded FK from the unified customer entity and expressed the relation through the normalized customer_account bridge.

conflicts.description: bank1 decomposes the domain into a separate bank entity referenced by branch, whereas bank2 has no bank table — a difference in level of entity decomposition.
conflicts.resolution: Kept 'bank' as a distinct resource with branch.bank_code referencing it; bank2 branches simply leave bank_code null.

conflicts.description: bank1 stores branch-to-loan and branch-to-account links as separate many-to-many tables, while bank2 stores single branch FKs on loan and account.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved bank1's many-to-many bridge tables (branch_loan, branch_account) alongside the direct FK columns on loan/account.

conflicts.description: Customer-account relationship is many-to-many in bank1 (hold_by) but modeled as 1:1 in bank2 (single account_id on customer).
conflicts.resolution: Resolved to many-to-many via the customer_account bridge, treating bank2's single FK as a restricted instance.

conflicts.description: Customer-loan relationship is many-to-many in both schemas, but bank2's 'borrower' adds a surrogate primary key and reifies the relation as an entity.
conflicts.resolution: Unified into a single many-to-many 'customer_loan' bridge keyed on (customer_id, loan_id), retaining the bank2 surrogate 'borrower_id' as a non-key attribute.

conflicts.description: Branch-loan is many-to-many (offer) in bank1 but many-to-one via a direct FK (loan.branch_id) in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Kept the branch_loan bridge for the M:N relation while preserving the direct loan.branch_id FK.

conflicts.description: Branch-account is many-to-many (maintain) in bank1 but many-to-one via a direct FK (account.branch_id) in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Kept the branch_account bridge while preserving the direct account.branch_id FK.

conflicts.description: bank2 introduces additional 1:1-style relationships (loan to account, credit card to account) not present in bank1, expanding relationship cardinalities across the unified model.
conflicts.resolution: Retained these as direct FK columns on their respective resources.

conflicts.description: Primary key of the customer entity is 'custid' in bank1 and 'customer_id' in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Unified primary key to 'customer_id' with both source keys listed in provenance.

conflicts.description: Primary key of the account entity is 'account_no' in bank1 and 'account_id' in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Unified primary key to 'account_id' with both source keys listed in provenance.

conflicts.description: Loan primary key is 'loan_id' in both schemas — consistent, but bank1 uses inconsistent casing in FK/PK declarations.
conflicts.resolution: Adopted 'loan_id' as the unified primary key.

conflicts.description: The customer-loan relation uses a composite key in bank1 but a synthetic surrogate primary key 'borrower_id' in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Adopted the composite key (customer_id, loan_id) for the unified customer_loan bridge, keeping borrower_id as a preserved surrogate attribute.

conflicts.description: bank1 identifies bank by a business code ('code') which is propagated as a foreign key on branch; bank2 has no equivalent key.
conflicts.resolution: Retained 'bank_code' as the bank primary key and as the branch foreign key.

conflicts.description: bank1 declares duplicate foreign keys using capitalized field names (Bank_Code, Branch_id, Loan_id, Account_No, Custid) that do not correspond to any declared columns — dangling/redundant key definitions.
conflicts.resolution: Consolidated each pair into a single canonical lowercase snake_case foreign key referencing the unified parent primary keys.

conflicts.description: Same customer identity attribute is named 'custid' in bank1 and 'customer_id' in bank2 (synonym divergence, and also the target PK of the merged customer entity).
conflicts.resolution: Unified to snake_case 'customer_id' as the target primary key of the customer resource.

conflicts.description: Customer name column is 'name' (bank1) vs 'customer_name' (bank2).
conflicts.resolution: Unified to 'name'.

conflicts.description: Customer telephone column named 'phone' (bank1) vs 'mobileno' (bank2).
conflicts.resolution: Unified to 'phone'; both represent the customer contact number.

conflicts.description: Account identifier named 'account_no' (bank1) vs 'account_id' (bank2).
conflicts.resolution: Unified to 'account_id' as the merged account primary key.

conflicts.description: Account type attribute named 'acc_type' (bank1) vs 'account_type' (bank2).
conflicts.resolution: Unified to 'account_type'.

conflicts.description: Account balance column named 'balance' (bank1) vs 'account_balance' (bank2).
conflicts.resolution: Unified to 'balance'.

conflicts.description: Branch name column named 'name' (bank1) vs 'branch_name' (bank2).
conflicts.resolution: Unified to 'name' inside the merged branch resource.

conflicts.description: Branch address column named 'address' (bank1) vs 'branch_address' (bank2).
conflicts.resolution: Unified to 'address' inside the merged branch resource.

conflicts.description: The bank identifier 'code' is a bare homonym for the parent bank key.
conflicts.resolution: Renamed to 'bank_code' to make the entity key explicit and consistent with the referencing column.

conflicts.description: Resource 'banker_info' and its 'banker_name' column diverge in naming style from the rest of the model.
conflicts.resolution: Resource renamed to 'banker' and 'banker_name' normalized to 'name'.

conflicts.description: bank1 uses verb-like association table names for its cross-entity links (offer, maintain, availed_by, hold_by).
conflicts.resolution: Retained meaningful association names offer/maintain for the branch links; renamed the merged person-loan and person-account links to the canonical 'customer_loan' and 'customer_account'.

conflicts.description: bank1 declares a second, PascalCase variant of each foreign key (Bank_Code, Branch_id, Custid, ...) that is a case-only homonym of the real column and points at non-existent PascalCase PKs.
conflicts.resolution: Treated as naming artifacts of the canonical lowercase columns and dropped; only one canonical FK per relationship is retained.

conflicts.description: Merged account balance is typed 'number' in bank1 but 'integer' in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Widened to 'number' (the superset) so both sources load without precision loss.

conflicts.description: Loan monetary columns are 'number' in bank1 but 'integer' in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized loan monetary columns to 'number' for cross-source homogeneity.

conflicts.description: Monetary columns declared as 'integer' in bank2 are inconsistent with the 'number' money representation chosen globally.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized to 'number' so all monetary attributes share one representation; 'assets' stays integer as a count.

conflicts.description: bank1 models a loan's value as a single 'amount', whereas bank2 decomposes it into the issued principal and the outstanding balance — related but not identical concepts.
conflicts.resolution: Kept as three distinct, semantically homogeneous attributes (amount, issued_amount, remaining_amount); 'amount' was NOT collapsed into 'issued_amount' because the exact same semantic attribute cannot be guaranteed.

conflicts.description: bank2 adds a 'branch.assets' quantitative attribute with no bank1 counterpart, and it is a monetary magnitude rather than an identifier.
conflicts.resolution: Retained as its own integer attribute on the merged branch resource; no other source column was mapped to it.

conflicts.description: bank1 normalizes cross-entity relationships into dedicated associative tables (offer, maintain, availed_by, hold_by), while bank2 embeds the same relationships as foreign-key columns inside entity tables (account.branch_id, loan.branch_id, customer.account_id) or as a surrogate-keyed link table (borrower).
conflicts.resolution: Normalized consistently: many-to-many relationships are kept as bridge resources (offer, maintain, customer_loan, customer_account) that reference parent entities exclusively through foreign keys; single-valued entity ownership links that both sources agree on (account.branch_id, loan.branch_id) are kept as entity foreign keys.

conflicts.description: bank2 denormalizes the customer-to-account link directly onto the customer entity, whereas bank1 keeps it in a separate relationship table.
conflicts.resolution: Folded into the customer_account bridge to avoid duplicating the relationship in two places.

conflicts.description: Customer-account relationship is many-to-many in bank1 (hold_by composite key) but many-to-one in bank2 (customer.account_id single FK).
conflicts.resolution: Unified to the more general N:M bridge 'customer_account' (composite PK customer_id, account_id), which subsumes bank2's N:1 usage.

conflicts.description: Both sources model customer-loan as a many-to-many association but with different structures (composite-key table vs surrogate-keyed entity).
conflicts.resolution: Merged into a single N:M bridge 'customer_loan' with composite PK (customer_id, loan_id).

conflicts.description: Branch-loan relationship appears as an N:M association (offer) in bank1 and as an N:1 ownership FK (loan.branch_id) in bank2; likewise bank1.maintain vs account.branch_id for branch-account.
conflicts.resolution: Both facets are semantically distinct (branch that offers/maintains vs branch that owns) and are each present in both sources, so the association (offer/maintain) and the ownership FK (branch_id) are retained as separate structures rather than collapsed.

conflicts.description: The customer-loan association uses a composite natural key in bank1 (custid, loan_id) but a synthetic surrogate key in bank2 (borrower_id).
conflicts.resolution: Unified on the composite natural key (customer_id, loan_id) for the merged customer_loan bridge; the bank2 surrogate borrower_id carries no source-independent counterpart and is dropped.

conflicts.description: bank1's foreign key declarations reference PascalCase key columns that do not exist as fields in the referenced resources, duplicating the valid lowercase FK declarations.
conflicts.resolution: Deduplicated to a single canonical FK per relationship, pointing at the merged snake_case primary keys.

conflicts.description: bank2 declares every foreign key twice (identical duplicate entries), indicating redundant key metadata.
conflicts.resolution: Deduplicated to one foreign-key declaration per relationship in the target schema.

conflicts.description: Primary key identification differs by naming and representation between sources for the two shared core entities.
conflicts.resolution: Each shared entity key unified to a single canonical PK (customer_id, account_id) whose provenance lists both source primary keys.

conflicts.description: Customer primary key is named 'custid' in bank1 but 'customer_id' in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Unified to 'customer_id' following the bank2 snake_case convention; both identifiers are grouped in the same column provenance.

conflicts.description: Customer name attribute named 'name' (bank1) vs 'customer_name' (bank2).
conflicts.resolution: Unified to 'name' as the atomic attribute name for the customer resource.

conflicts.description: Contact number stored as 'phone' (bank1) vs 'mobileno' (bank2).
conflicts.resolution: Unified to 'phone' as the canonical mobile/telephone attribute.

conflicts.description: Branch label named 'name' (bank1) vs 'branch_name' (bank2).
conflicts.resolution: Unified to 'name' within the branch resource.

conflicts.description: Branch address named 'address' (bank1) vs 'branch_address' (bank2).
conflicts.resolution: Unified to 'address' within the branch resource.

conflicts.description: Account type attribute abbreviated as 'acc_type' (bank1) vs 'account_type' (bank2).
conflicts.resolution: Unified to 'account_type' using the fully spelled snake_case name.

conflicts.description: Account balance named 'balance' (bank1) vs 'account_balance' (bank2).
conflicts.resolution: Unified to 'balance' within the account resource.

conflicts.description: Account identifier named 'account_no' (bank1) vs 'account_id' (bank2).
conflicts.resolution: Unified to 'account_id' as the account primary key column name.

conflicts.description: Resource 'banker_info' and column 'banker_name' carry redundant entity prefixes relative to the target naming scheme.
conflicts.resolution: Resource renamed to 'banker' and column to 'name' for a normalized, consistent naming convention.

conflicts.description: Relationship resources use heterogeneous, verb-based names (hold_by, availed_by, maintain, offer) in bank1 while bank2 names the analogous bridge 'borrower' as if it were an entity.
conflicts.resolution: Bridge resources renamed to a consistent composite <entity>_<entity> convention (customer_account, customer_loan, branch_account, branch_loan).

conflicts.description: Resource named 'customer_credit_card' embeds the parent entity name prefix.
conflicts.resolution: Renamed to 'credit_card'; the customer linkage is captured through the customer_id foreign key.

conflicts.description: Account balance is declared 'number' in bank1 but 'integer' in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Promoted to 'number' to preserve fractional monetary precision without loss across both sources.

conflicts.description: Loan principal is 'number' in bank1 but 'integer' in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Promoted to 'number' so the unified 'issued_amount' column accommodates both representations.

conflicts.description: All bank2 monetary/quantitative attributes (transaction amount, loan payment amount, card limit, branch assets) are declared 'integer', whereas bank1 monetary attributes use 'number'.
conflicts.resolution: Monetary measures normalized to 'number'; 'assets' retained as 'integer' since it is a count-like magnitude only present in bank2.

conflicts.description: Both columns denote the loan principal, but bank1 labels it generically as 'amount' while bank2 distinguishes 'issued_amount' from 'remaining_amount'.
conflicts.resolution: Merged into 'issued_amount' as the single principal-amount attribute; the assumption that bank1 'amount' equals the issued principal is documented, and 'remaining_amount' is kept as a distinct attribute.

conflicts.description: Monetary scale representation differs: bank2 models money as whole-number integers while bank1 permits decimal numbers, implying different implicit precision/scale (e.g., whole currency units vs. fractional).
conflicts.resolution: All monetary quantities unified to the 'number' type so a single decimal currency unit convention applies across the global schema.

conflicts.description: Categorical account-type values may follow different domain encodings between the two sources.
conflicts.resolution: Both mapped to a single 'account_type' string attribute; value-level harmonization is deferred to the transformation layer.

conflicts.description: The customer-account linkage is modeled as an explicit many-to-many bridge (hold_by) in bank1, but embedded as a single FK attribute (account_id) on the customer table in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized into a dedicated bridge resource 'customer_account' with composite key (customer_id, account_id), preserving both the bank1 bridge rows and the bank2 embedded linkage.

conflicts.description: The same customer-loan relationship is represented by two separate bridge structures with different naming and key strategies.
conflicts.resolution: Unified into one bridge resource 'customer_loan' (customer_id, loan_id), merging provenance from availed_by and borrower.

conflicts.description: Branch-loan association exists simultaneously as an explicit bridge (offer) and as a direct FK (loan.branch_id) in bank1, while bank2 only uses the direct FK.
conflicts.resolution: Both representations retained: 'branch_loan' bridge preserves the M:N association and 'loan.branch_id' preserves the direct FK.

conflicts.description: Branch-account association exists as both an explicit bridge (maintain) and a direct FK in bank1, while bank2 relies only on the direct FK.
conflicts.resolution: Both representations retained: 'branch_account' bridge preserves the M:N association and 'account.branch_id' preserves the direct FK.

conflicts.description: bank1 decomposes an explicit 'bank' parent entity referenced by branch.bank_code, whereas bank2 has no bank entity and instead stores branch-level 'assets'.
conflicts.resolution: The 'bank' entity is retained as a top-level resource and branch.bank_code is preserved as an optional FK; the bank2-only 'assets' attribute is added to the unified branch resource.

conflicts.description: bank2 embeds account linkage directly inside customer and loan, mixing associative relationships into entity tables.
conflicts.resolution: Account relationships re-expressed through normalized FK/bridge columns so entity tables hold only atomic attributes.

conflicts.description: Customer-account relationship is many-to-many in bank1 (via hold_by) but one-to-many/one-to-one in bank2 (account_id on customer).
conflicts.resolution: Resolved to a many-to-many bridge 'customer_account' to safely accommodate both cardinalities.

conflicts.description: bank1 expresses the branch-loan relationship as both M:N (offer) and N:1 (loan.branch_id), which is redundant; bank2 expresses it only as N:1.
conflicts.resolution: N:1 enforced via loan.branch_id; the residual M:N is retained explicitly as 'branch_loan' so no source association is discarded.

conflicts.description: Both sources model the customer-loan linkage as M:N, but bank2 decorates the bridge with an extra surrogate identity while bank1 uses the natural pair.
conflicts.resolution: Unified to a single M:N bridge 'customer_loan' keyed on the natural pair (customer_id, loan_id).

conflicts.description: bank1 identifies the bank entity with a string natural key 'code', while branches (and all other entities) use integer surrogate keys.
conflicts.resolution: Bank key retained as the string primary key 'bank_code'; it is referenced by an optional FK from branch without altering the integer surrogate keys used elsewhere.

conflicts.description: bank1 bridge tables are keyed by natural composite keys, whereas bank2.borrower introduces a surrogate 'borrower_id' primary key in addition to its natural (customer_id, loan_id) pair.
conflicts.resolution: All bridges unified on natural composite primary keys; the bank2 surrogate borrower_id is dropped as redundant, with the natural key columns carrying provenance.

conflicts.description: bank1 declares the same foreign key twice using inconsistent casing (e.g., bank_code/Bank_Code, branch_id/Branch_id), implying duplicate or phantom key references.
conflicts.resolution: De-duplicated into single, consistently snake_case foreign keys; the casing variants are consolidated into the lowercase column provenance.

conflicts.description: bank2 restates identical foreign key declarations twice per relationship (exact duplicates).
conflicts.resolution: Collapsed to a single foreign key definition per relationship in the unified schema.

conflicts.description: bank2 defines account_id as a mandatory foreign key on customer, creating a key dependency in the opposite direction of bank1's customer->account bridge.
conflicts.resolution: Customer-to-account dependency re-expressed as the 'customer_account' bridge, removing the embedded FK from the customer entity.

conflicts.description: Synonymous entities and attributes representing films/titles: 'title_basics' in IMDb vs 'film' in Sakila; 'primarytitle' / 'originaltitle' vs 'title'; 'runtimeminutes' vs 'length'; 'startyear' vs 'release_year'.
conflicts.resolution: Harmonized into unified tables 'title' and related entities using standardized snake_case attribute names such as 'title', 'runtime_minutes', and 'release_year'.

conflicts.description: Synonymous person/actor entities and attributes: 'name_basics' in IMDb vs 'actor' in Sakila; 'primaryname' vs 'first_name' / 'last_name'.
conflicts.resolution: Created a unified 'person' table accommodating both full names and separate first/last name components, as well as preserving specific actor relations.

conflicts.description: Identifier and numerical type mismatches: IMDb identifiers (nconst, tconst) are represented as numbers in the source schema metadata despite being alphanumeric strings (tconst/nconst), whereas Sakila uses string surrogate keys. Similarly, IMDb primarytitle is typed as integer despite being text, and Sakila length, rental_duration, rental_rate, and replacement_cost are typed as string.
conflicts.resolution: Unified alphanumeric identifiers and textual fields as strings, and standardized numerical attributes (such as runtime_minutes and financial costs) to integer/number.

conflicts.description: Boolean representation differences: boolean flags such as IMDb 'isadult' / 'isoriginaltitle' vs Sakila customer/staff 'active' encoded as strings ('TRUE'/'FALSE').
conflicts.resolution: Standardized all boolean flag indicators to the generic boolean type.

conflicts.description: Semantic scope difference in film ratings: IMDb ratings ('averagerating' and 'numvotes') represent weighted average user scores and review volume, whereas Sakila 'rating' represents MPAA parental guidance age certification (G, PG, PG-13, R, NC-17).
conflicts.resolution: Segregated MPAA content rating into 'mpaa_rating' on the title entity and retained community aggregate rating metrics within a distinct title rating structure.

conflicts.description: Name representations: IMDb uses a single composite string 'primaryname', while Sakila stores 'first_name' and 'last_name'.
conflicts.resolution: Modeled atomic first and last name fields alongside a consolidated full/primary name field in the person resource.

conflicts.description: Denormalized delimited multi-value fields in IMDb (genres in title_basics, knownfortitles and primaryprofession in name_basics, directors and writers in title_crew) versus normalized relational bridge tables in Sakila (film_category, film_actor).
conflicts.resolution: Normalized non-atomic string arrays into dedicated first-class entities and relational bridge tables (e.g., genre/title_genre, person_profession, title_crew_role, title_known_for).

conflicts.description: IMDb title_principals conflates cast and crew roles, character appearances, and ordering in a single table, whereas Sakila isolates film_actor.
conflicts.resolution: Designed a normalized title_cast_crew junction table that accommodates cast/crew categories, specific job titles, played characters, and billing ordering.

conflicts.description: Relationship cardinality between films and categories/genres: IMDb embeds a bounded list (up to 3 genres) per title row, while Sakila supports an arbitrary N:M relation between film and category.
conflicts.resolution: Adopted an N:M associative table 'title_category' linking titles and canonical categories/genres to support arbitrary cardinality.

conflicts.description: Primary key identification disparities between IMDb and Sakila for titles and persons: IMDb uses global alphanumeric authority identifiers (tconst, nconst), while Sakila uses localized integer/string surrogate keys (film_id, actor_id).
conflicts.resolution: Defined unified entity tables with canonical synthetic primary keys (e.g. title_id, person_id) and mapped the source keys into source_provenance accordingly.

conflicts.description: Different table and attribute naming conventions between IMDB and Sakila: IMDB uses 'name_basics' for people and 'title_basics' for movies/shows, whereas Sakila uses 'actor' and 'film'. Similarly, IMDB uses 'primarytitle'/'originaltitle' and Sakila uses 'title'.
conflicts.resolution: Adopt standardized, snake_case canonical entity and attribute names such as 'person', 'title', and unified title/name fields.

conflicts.description: Film duration is represented as 'runtimeminutes' in IMDB and 'length' in Sakila.
conflicts.resolution: Harmonize runtime column name to 'runtime_minutes'.

conflicts.description: Release year is represented as 'startyear' in IMDB title_basics and 'release_year' in Sakila film.
conflicts.resolution: Map both attributes to a canonical 'release_year' field in the unified title resource.

conflicts.description: Data type differences for identifiers: IMDB defines 'tconst' and 'nconst' as number (while descriptions state alphanumeric string), whereas Sakila uses string for 'film_id' and 'actor_id'. Similarly, IMDB 'primarytitle' is typed as integer despite being title text.
conflicts.resolution: Unify all identifier fields and title text fields to generic string type.

conflicts.description: Runtime duration is typed as integer in IMDB ('runtimeminutes') and string in Sakila ('length').
conflicts.resolution: Standardize runtime duration to integer.

conflicts.description: Active flags in Sakila ('active' in customer and staff) are typed as string, whereas boolean flags like 'isadult' in IMDB are boolean.
conflicts.resolution: Convert boolean/flag attributes to generic Frictionless boolean type.

conflicts.description: Temporal fields such as 'last_update', 'rental_date', and 'payment_date' are typed as date in Sakila, but timestamp data requires datetime representation.
conflicts.resolution: Standardize point-in-time event timestamps to datetime.

conflicts.description: Name representation: IMDB name_basics provides 'primaryname' as a single string, whereas Sakila actor/customer/staff splits names into 'first_name' and 'last_name'.
conflicts.resolution: Maintain atomic name attributes ('first_name', 'last_name') while also capturing full name ('primary_name') for compatibility.

conflicts.description: Rating semantics: Sakila 'film.rating' denotes MPAA content advisory rating (G, PG, R, etc.), whereas IMDB 'title_ratings' represents community user feedback ratings ('averagerating' and 'numvotes').
conflicts.resolution: Model MPAA rating as 'content_rating' in the title table, and isolate community user review metrics in title_rating to preserve semantic separation.

conflicts.description: Genre/Category representation: IMDB stores genres as a delimited/array string in 'title_basics.genres', whereas Sakila models categories via normalized bridge tables ('category' and 'film_category').
conflicts.resolution: Adopt a normalized relational schema with a unified 'category' entity and 'title_category' bridge table.

conflicts.description: Crew and cast representation: IMDB title_crew stores arrays of nconsts for directors and writers, and title_principals links titles and people with roles/characters, while Sakila uses a film_actor bridge table.
conflicts.resolution: Normalize cast and crew associations into 'title_principal' and specific participation bridge tables, eliminating delimited string arrays.

conflicts.description: Person entity scope: Sakila decomposes people into separate tables ('actor', 'customer', 'staff'), whereas IMDB maintains a unified 'name_basics' table for all industry persons.
conflicts.resolution: Maintain unified core entity 'person' while retaining Sakila business operational entities ('customer', 'staff') linked via appropriate relationships.

conflicts.description: Title to language mapping: IMDB title_akas allows multiple localized titles with language and region per title (1:N), whereas Sakila film references a single language_id and original_language_id (N:1).
conflicts.resolution: Retain language foreign keys on the title entity for primary/original language, and retain the title_alias (title_akas) resource to support 1:N localized language editions.

conflicts.description: IMDB title_akas, title_crew, title_episode, title_principals, and title_ratings lack formal primary keys in the source schema, relying on implicit compound keys.
conflicts.resolution: Introduce explicit primary keys (synthetic surrogate keys or composite natural keys) across all normalized target resources.

conflicts.description: Different naming conventions between IMDb (camelCase/concatenated lowercase, e.g. 'title_basics', 'primarytitle', 'runtimeminutes') and Sakila (snake_case, e.g. 'film', 'title', 'length').
conflicts.resolution: Adopted uniform snake_case across all global schema entities and fields (e.g., 'title' instead of 'primarytitle'/'title', 'runtime_minutes' instead of 'runtimeminutes'/'length').

conflicts.description: Synonymous entity names representing film and media metadata: IMDb uses 'title_basics' while Sakila uses 'film'.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized media title entity as 'film_work' to unify films, series, and video productions.

conflicts.description: Synonymous entity names representing people involved in media: IMDb uses 'name_basics' for cast and crew, while Sakila isolates actors into 'actor'.
conflicts.resolution: Unified individual persons into a comprehensive 'person' entity.

conflicts.description: Primary and foreign keys in IMDb are modeled as 'number' (despite tconst/nconst descriptions noting alphanumeric strings), whereas Sakila models IDs as 'string'. Additionally, 'primarytitle' in IMDb is typed as integer despite being a text title.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized all alphanumeric identity codes and names as generic 'string' types.

conflicts.description: Duration/runtime is typed as 'integer' in IMDb ('runtimeminutes') and 'string' in Sakila ('length'). Release year is 'string' in both or represented as dates/years.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized duration into an integer representing minutes ('runtime_minutes') and release year as integer ('release_year').

conflicts.description: Active status indicator in Sakila customer/staff is stored as string ('TRUE'/'FALSE'), whereas IMDb uses boolean.
conflicts.resolution: Harmonized boolean attributes to generic frictionless 'boolean' type.

conflicts.description: Person names in IMDb are kept in a single combined field ('primaryname'), whereas Sakila splits actor names into 'first_name' and 'last_name'.
conflicts.resolution: Retained both atomic 'first_name' and 'last_name' fields alongside full 'name' to preserve granular data from Sakila while accommodating consolidated IMDb names.

conflicts.description: Rating in Sakila represents MPAA content advisory ratings (G, PG, PG-13, R, NC-17), while IMDb records an adult flag ('isadult') and numeric weighted average scores ('averagerating').
conflicts.resolution: Maintained distinct target attributes for content rating code ('mpaa_rating'), adult content flag ('is_adult'), and user review scores.

conflicts.description: IMDb denormalizes genres into a comma-delimited string in 'title_basics.genres', while Sakila models categories/genres in a normalized many-to-many relationship ('film_category' and 'category').
conflicts.resolution: Normalized genres into relational entities: 'genre' (for unique genres/categories) and 'film_work_genre' (as the associative bridge table).

conflicts.description: IMDb stores title principals and crew roles in dedicated casting/crew tables ('title_principals', 'title_crew'), whereas Sakila uses 'film_actor' strictly for acting roles.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized production participants into a unified 'film_work_participant' bridge table capturing the person, film, and role/category.

conflicts.description: IMDb represents multi-valued attributes like 'knownfortitles' and 'primaryprofession' as delimited string arrays within the 'name_basics' record.
conflicts.resolution: Extracted multi-valued person attributes into normalized child/bridge tables or normalized association structures.

conflicts.description: Primary keys for films ('tconst' vs 'film_id') and people ('nconst' vs 'actor_id') use distinct identifier domains and surrogate mechanisms.
conflicts.resolution: Created unified entity primary keys with mapping source provenance tracking respective source keys, harmonized to string format.

conflicts.description: The same broad audiovisual-work concept is named title in IMDb and film in Sakila, with different identifier names.
conflicts.resolution: Unified both under the work entity with snake_case work terminology and source-scoped work identifiers.

conflicts.description: IMDb represents a credited person name as primaryname, while Sakila calls the entity actor and separates first and last names.
conflicts.resolution: Unified the entity as person while retaining display_name separately from atomic given_name and family_name.

conflicts.description: IMDb uses genre terminology while Sakila uses category for a comparable film classification concept.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized the concept as genre and preserved source category identifiers as genre identifiers.

conflicts.description: The source term inventory identifies an individual physical copy rather than an aggregate stock measure.
conflicts.resolution: Renamed the target entity and key to inventory_item and inventory_item_id.

conflicts.description: IMDb alphanumeric identifiers are declared as number even though their descriptions define string identifiers.
conflicts.resolution: Typed all IMDb identifiers as string in the target.

conflicts.description: IMDb primarytitle is declared integer but described as title text.
conflicts.resolution: Typed primary_title as string.

conflicts.description: Calendar years are represented as strings in the sources.
conflicts.resolution: Typed year attributes as integer, treating source null markers as null values.

conflicts.description: Numeric durations and monetary values are declared as strings.
conflicts.resolution: Typed durations as integer quantities and monetary values as number.

conflicts.description: Logical active flags are declared as strings.
conflicts.resolution: Typed active-state fields as boolean.

conflicts.description: Fields described as containing date and time are declared as date.
conflicts.resolution: Typed event and update timestamps as datetime.

conflicts.description: Runtime is represented in minutes in both sources, which is not the selected standard SI duration unit.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized runtime as runtime_seconds.

conflicts.description: Rental duration is represented in days.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized the rental period as seconds.

conflicts.description: IMDb average rating is a numeric user score, whereas Sakila rating is a categorical audience classification.
conflicts.resolution: Kept these as separate average_rating and content_rating attributes rather than conflating their scales.

conflicts.description: Primary/display titles and original-language titles have distinct semantics despite all being title text.
conflicts.resolution: Mapped display titles to primary_title and retained original_title as a separate attribute.

conflicts.description: Current release language, original work language, and alternate-title language play different semantic roles.
conflicts.resolution: Retained distinct foreign-key roles on work and alternate_title while sharing a normalized language entity.

conflicts.description: Monetary values lack an explicit source currency.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved numeric amounts without inventing a currency code and documented reliance on the source system currency.

conflicts.description: Multiple source columns encode arrays or multi-value attributes inside strings.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized each multi-value attribute into child or bridge resources with atomic values and explicit foreign keys.

conflicts.description: Sakila duplicates searchable film text in film_text while core film attributes reside in film.
conflicts.resolution: Merged duplicate title and description attributes into work with provenance from both tables.

conflicts.description: IMDb models title metadata only, while Sakila separates catalog works, physical copies, and rental transactions.
conflicts.resolution: Retained normalized work, inventory_item, and rental entities so catalog identity is not conflated with physical-copy or transaction identity.

conflicts.description: The address location is an opaque geometry value whose internal geometry kind and components are unspecified.
conflicts.resolution: Retained it as a single serialized geometry field rather than inventing latitude/longitude semantics not supplied by the source.

conflicts.description: IMDb embeds up to several genres per title, whereas Sakila expresses film categories through a many-to-many bridge.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized both as the many-to-many work_genre relationship.

conflicts.description: IMDb embeds multiple directors and writers in one crew row, while Sakila uses rows in a film-actor bridge.
conflicts.resolution: Exploded IMDb arrays into work_director and work_writer bridges and represented principal/cast associations in work_credit.

conflicts.description: A person can be known for several works and a work can be associated with several persons.
conflicts.resolution: Created the many-to-many person_known_work bridge.

conflicts.description: Episodes and series are both titles linked by a recursive one-to-many relationship.
conflicts.resolution: Created episode as a relationship resource with separate episode and parent-series foreign keys to work.

conflicts.description: One catalog film can have many physical inventory copies.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved work-to-inventory_item as a one-to-many relationship.

conflicts.description: Equivalent work entities use incompatible natural-looking alphanumeric and surrogate identifiers, and film_text omits an explicit key declaration.
conflicts.resolution: Defined source-scoped string work_id as the unified key and included all corresponding source identifiers in its provenance.

conflicts.description: Equivalent credited-person entities use different identifier systems.
conflicts.resolution: Defined a source-scoped string person_id with both source primary keys in provenance.

conflicts.description: IMDb alternate titles have no declared primary key although ordering is unique only within a title.
conflicts.resolution: Introduced a synthetic alternate_title_id and retained ordering as a non-identity sequence attribute.

conflicts.description: Credit rows have no common declared key; IMDb uses per-title ordering while Sakila identifies associations through foreign-key pairs.
conflicts.resolution: Introduced a synthetic credit_id so source-specific sequence and relationship keys remain semantically separate.

conflicts.description: Sakila provides a payment identifier described as a surrogate key but does not declare a table primary key.
conflicts.resolution: Promoted payment_id to the target payment primary key.

conflicts.description: Sakila bridge tables declare no primary keys despite representing unique entity associations.
conflicts.resolution: Used the corresponding foreign-key pairs as composite target keys where the association has no additional row identity.
