conflicts.description: The same human subject entity is named patients in Synthea and person in OMOP, with differing attribute names such as birthdate versus birth_datetime.
conflicts.resolution: Adopted the singular canonical resource person and descriptive snake_case field names while retaining exact source provenance.

conflicts.description: Synthea encounter and OMOP visit occurrence represent the same high-level care interaction under different terminology.
conflicts.resolution: Unified both as visit; OMOP visit detail remains a finer-grained source structure rather than being conflated with the encounter identity.

conflicts.description: Equivalent provider specialty attributes use a misspelling and different naming conventions.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized the target name to specialty_source_value.

conflicts.description: Several Synthea imaging columns contain spaces and violate target naming conventions.
conflicts.resolution: Converted all target identifiers to snake_case without changing their semantics.

conflicts.description: Monetary amounts are mostly declared as strings, despite representing numeric quantities.
conflicts.resolution: Represented monetary amounts as number and retained currency separately through a concept identifier.

conflicts.description: Counts are represented as strings in multiple source structures.
conflicts.resolution: Canonical count attributes use integer.

conflicts.description: Synthea declares the value datatype as number while storing the actual result as string; OMOP separates typed result columns.
conflicts.resolution: Used separate numeric, string, and concept-valued result fields and retained the source datatype declaration independently.

conflicts.description: Fields described as date-times are declared as date in both source schemas.
conflicts.resolution: Canonical event timestamps use datetime, while genuinely date-only attributes remain date.

conflicts.description: Invalidation reason codes are incorrectly typed as date in several OMOP resources.
conflicts.resolution: Canonical invalidation reason attributes use string.

conflicts.description: Textual values are incorrectly declared as integer.
conflicts.resolution: Canonical names and prescription directions use string.

conflicts.description: Coordinates are declared as strings.
conflicts.resolution: Coordinates use number in decimal degrees.

conflicts.description: Synthea stores a SNOMED source code directly, whereas OMOP distinguishes a standardized concept identifier from the verbatim source code.
conflicts.resolution: Kept standardized concept identity and source code in separate fields; no source code was treated as an OMOP concept identifier without vocabulary mapping.

conflicts.description: Units may be free text, source codes, or standardized concepts and may use non-SI scales.
conflicts.resolution: Retained verbatim units separately and defined numeric physical results to be normalized to the applicable SI unit, with the standardized unit concept recording the normalized unit.

conflicts.description: Synthea uses compact M/F encoding while OMOP distinguishes source values from standardized concepts.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved source encoding in gender_source_value and kept the standardized concept in a distinct foreign key.

conflicts.description: The Synthea encounter field named provider semantically references an organization, while OMOP provider_id references a clinician.
conflicts.resolution: Mapped the Synthea field only to care_site_id and kept clinician provider_id semantically separate.

conflicts.description: Medication codes use RxNorm, immunization codes use CVX, and OMOP drug source values can use multiple vocabularies.
conflicts.resolution: Unified them as drug exposures but retained the source code and an explicit exposure category; standardized concept assignment remains vocabulary-aware.

conflicts.description: Synthea cost is a base or line-item amount, while OMOP distinguishes charged, incurred, and paid amounts.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved Synthea amounts as source_cost_amount and kept OMOP financial measures separate rather than asserting false equivalence.

conflicts.description: Synthea repeats address attributes inside person, organization, and provider tables, while OMOP normalizes addresses into location.
conflicts.resolution: Adopted a normalized location resource referenced by people and care sites; provider location can be represented through its care site.

conflicts.description: Multiple identifier types are stored as separate columns on the patient record.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized identifiers into person_identifier with one atomic identifier type and value per row.

conflicts.description: Synthea combines laboratory measurements and observations, while OMOP decomposes them into domain-specific tables.
conflicts.resolution: Created a common clinical_observation resource with an explicit observation_kind discriminator and typed values.

conflicts.description: Synthea separates immunizations from medications, while OMOP can represent administrations in drug exposure.
conflicts.resolution: Unified both event forms in drug_exposure and preserved their category explicitly.

conflicts.description: Synthea embeds costs on clinical event rows, while OMOP stores cost in a separate polymorphic resource.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized all financial values into cost, linked conceptually to the applicable clinical event.

conflicts.description: OMOP supports a two-level visit hierarchy, whereas Synthea provides only a single encounter level.
conflicts.resolution: Used visit as the common encounter level; OMOP visit-detail hierarchy is retained as optional finer-grained information rather than merged into unrelated event identifiers.

conflicts.description: Embedded source addresses imply one address snapshot per entity row, while a normalized location may be shared by many entities.
conflicts.resolution: Modeled many people or care sites to one location through foreign keys and avoided embedding composite addresses.

conflicts.description: The wide Synthea patient row limits each identifier category to at most one value, while identifiers are conceptually repeatable.
conflicts.resolution: Modeled person to person_identifier as one-to-many.

conflicts.description: Synthea has one encounter level, while OMOP permits one visit occurrence to contain many visit details.
conflicts.resolution: Kept the common visit grain and treated detail records as optional children when that OMOP granularity is needed.

conflicts.description: A source observation has one polymorphic result, represented through different physical columns in OMOP.
conflicts.resolution: Retained mutually exclusive typed value columns on one clinical observation row rather than creating multiple observation rows.

conflicts.description: Several OMOP resources use polymorphic references that can target multiple entity domains and cannot be represented by one ordinary foreign key.
conflicts.resolution: Kept domain/type metadata conceptually separate from event identifiers and did not collapse polymorphic identifiers into person, provider, or visit foreign keys.

conflicts.description: Equivalent person entities use different primary-key names, and Synthea does not formally declare its documented key.
conflicts.resolution: Defined person_id as the required primary key with provenance from both source identifiers.

conflicts.description: Equivalent encounter entities use differently named identifiers and only OMOP formally declares the key.
conflicts.resolution: Defined visit_id as the unified primary key with provenance from both source identifiers.

conflicts.description: Organization and care-site identifiers name the same facility identity differently.
conflicts.resolution: Defined care_site_id as the unified facility key with provenance from both sources.

conflicts.description: Several Synthea event tables have no declared or documented event key, while corresponding OMOP resources have event identifiers that are not consistently declared as primary keys.
conflicts.resolution: Established required target event keys; OMOP identifiers supply provenance where present, and deterministic surrogate values are generated for keyless source rows.

conflicts.description: The name provider is a foreign-key homonym: it points to an organization in Synthea encounters but to a clinician in OMOP visits.
conflicts.resolution: Defined separate care_site_id and provider_id foreign keys and never combined their provenance.

conflicts.description: OMOP polymorphic event identifiers do not reference a single declared resource key.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved domain/type discriminators with polymorphic identifiers and avoided declaring invalid ordinary foreign keys.

conflicts.description: The same patient entity is named patients in Synthea and person in OMOP, with corresponding attribute synonyms such as id/person_id, birthdate/birth_datetime, and gender/gender_source_value.
conflicts.resolution: Adopted the singular canonical person resource and explicit snake_case attribute names while retaining standard-concept and source-value representations separately.

conflicts.description: Synthea calls a care interaction an encounter while OMOP calls the comparable top-level event a visit occurrence.
conflicts.resolution: Adopted encounter as the canonical business term and aligned only semantically equivalent top-level visit attributes.

conflicts.description: Provider specialty uses a misspelled Synthea column and OMOP source-value terminology.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized the target spelling to specialty and retained separate standard-concept and source-value columns.

conflicts.description: Several Synthea field names contain spaces and are not snake_case.
conflicts.resolution: Renamed them to atomic snake_case source-value and description fields.

conflicts.description: Monetary values are represented primarily as strings, despite being quantitative amounts.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized monetary amounts to number; currency remains an independent concept attribute.

conflicts.description: Synthea declares observation type as number even though it describes a datatype, and stores heterogeneous result values in one string column; OMOP separates numeric, text, and concept results.
conflicts.resolution: Represented the datatype indicator as string and split results into numeric, textual, concept, and verbatim source-value fields.

conflicts.description: Fields described as timestamps are typed as date in both sources.
conflicts.resolution: Used datetime for canonical event timestamps while allowing date-only source precision.

conflicts.description: Invalidation reason flags are incorrectly typed as date in several OMOP resources.
conflicts.resolution: Modeled invalidation reasons as strings and kept validity dates in separate date fields.

conflicts.description: Coordinates and numeric reference-range limits are represented as strings.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized these quantitative values to number.

conflicts.description: Textual values are incorrectly declared as integer in the source schema.
conflicts.resolution: Canonical textual counterparts use string; composite NLP modifiers should be normalized when those extensions are materialized.

conflicts.description: Synthea code columns contain vocabulary-native codes, whereas OMOP distinguishes globally unique standard concept identifiers from verbatim source codes.
conflicts.resolution: Kept standard concept identifiers, source concept identifiers, and source values as distinct semantic attributes; vocabulary-native codes were never merged directly into concept IDs.

conflicts.description: Units may be free text in Synthea but standardized concepts plus source text in OMOP, and physical quantities may use non-SI scales.
conflicts.resolution: Retained both standard unit concepts and source unit text; canonical numeric values and ranges are to be expressed in compatible SI units where a valid conversion exists.

conflicts.description: The Synthea encounter provider field is documented as an organization foreign key, while OMOP provider_id identifies a clinician.
conflicts.resolution: Mapped Synthea encounters.provider only to care_site_id and kept clinician provider_id semantically separate.

conflicts.description: Synthea uses compact M/F source encoding while OMOP distinguishes source encoding from standardized gender concepts.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved the source value and provided a separate FK to the standardized concept.

conflicts.description: Synthea base or line-item cost does not specify whether the amount is a charge, provider cost, or paid amount, while OMOP distinguishes these semantics.
conflicts.resolution: Stored Synthea amounts in a dedicated base_or_line_item_amount field and did not merge them with OMOP total charge, cost, or paid fields.

conflicts.description: Synthea repeats address attributes in entity tables, while OMOP normalizes geographic data into location.
conflicts.resolution: Adopted a normalized location resource and location foreign keys; generated location identifiers are used where Synthea has no source location key.

conflicts.description: Synthea combines labs and general observations in one table, while OMOP decomposes them into observation and measurement domains.
conflicts.resolution: Created one canonical clinical_observation resource with an explicit domain discriminator and homogeneous result fields, preserving the source domain without conflating identifiers.

conflicts.description: Synthea embeds cost on clinical event rows, while OMOP stores costs in a separate event-linked table.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized costs into event_cost so each monetary record is related to its clinical event rather than embedded in multiple event structures.

conflicts.description: Synthea embeds death date in the patient row, while OMOP uses a separate death resource with cause and provenance attributes.
conflicts.resolution: Placed the shared death date on person for the core unified view; OMOP-specific cause and death-provenance details remain separable extensions and are not conflated with demographics.

conflicts.description: Synthea provides a dedicated imaging-study structure, whereas OMOP can represent imaging through multiple clinical domains and lacks a directly equivalent study-series table in the supplied package.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved imaging_study as a dedicated normalized resource rather than forcing non-equivalent OMOP event fields into it.

conflicts.description: Synthea has one encounter level, whereas OMOP supports a visit occurrence with zero or more nested visit details.
conflicts.resolution: Unified Synthea encounters with the top-level OMOP visit occurrence; nested visit details remain a subordinate extension and are not merged into the encounter identity.

conflicts.description: Both models support many providers per organization/care site, but Synthea embeds addresses on both entities while OMOP generally associates providers with a care site.
conflicts.resolution: Modeled provider-to-care-site as N:1 and separated optional provider and care-site locations.

conflicts.description: A person and encounter can have many heterogeneous result records; source decomposition differs by domain.
conflicts.resolution: Used a 1:N relationship from person and encounter to clinical_observation, with one row per atomic result.

conflicts.description: OMOP contains multiple many-to-many semantic and fact relationship structures with directional roles.
conflicts.resolution: These relationship roles must remain bridge structures with separate source and destination foreign keys; their identifiers are never coalesced into one provenance-bearing field.

conflicts.description: Several Synthea event tables declare no primary key, while comparable OMOP event tables contain event identifiers that are not consistently declared as primary keys in the supplied package.
conflicts.resolution: Declared canonical event primary keys; used OMOP identifiers where available and synthetic keys only for Synthea rows without source identifiers.

conflicts.description: Equivalent person identities use different key names.
conflicts.resolution: Unified them as person.person_id and listed both source primary-key columns in provenance.

conflicts.description: Equivalent top-level encounter identities use different key names.
conflicts.resolution: Unified them as encounter.encounter_id and listed both source keys in provenance.

conflicts.description: Identically suggestive foreign-key names refer to different entity types: organization in Synthea and clinician in OMOP.
conflicts.resolution: Kept care_site_id and provider_id as separate foreign keys and prohibited identity coalescence.

conflicts.description: Several OMOP fields are polymorphic references whose target table is determined by an accompanying domain or field concept rather than a conventional foreign key.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved the conceptual polymorphism for extension resources and did not incorrectly declare these IDs as foreign keys to one canonical entity.

conflicts.description: The same human subject entity is named patients in Synthea and person in OMOP, with differing field names such as id/person_id, first/given name, last/family name, and zip/postal code.
conflicts.resolution: Adopted singular, snake_case canonical resources and explicit semantic field names, including person, given_name, family_name, and postal_code.

conflicts.description: Synthea uses encounter terminology while OMOP uses visit occurrence terminology for the same high-level care interaction.
conflicts.resolution: Unified the high-level entity as encounter while retaining OMOP-specific nested visit detail in encounter_detail.

conflicts.description: The provider specialty attribute has spelling and naming differences.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized the verbatim attribute name to specialty_source_value and retained standardized specialty separately.

conflicts.description: Several Synthea columns contain spaces and are not snake_case.
conflicts.resolution: Renamed all target fields to snake_case without changing their semantics.

conflicts.description: Monetary quantities are represented as strings in both sources despite being numeric amounts.
conflicts.resolution: Represented monetary amounts as number and separated ambiguous Synthea base or line-item amounts from OMOP's explicitly classified charge, cost, and paid amounts.

conflicts.description: Counts are represented as strings in source schemas.
conflicts.resolution: Canonical count fields use integer.

conflicts.description: Synthea declares the value datatype indicator as number and stores all result values as string, while OMOP separates numeric, string, and concept-valued results.
conflicts.resolution: Used typed, atomic result columns and retained a verbatim source value; numeric conversion is represented only in numeric value fields.

conflicts.description: Several OMOP columns have source types inconsistent with their descriptions, including categorical invalidation reasons typed as date, a vocabulary name typed as integer, prescription text typed as integer, and birth components typed as date.
conflicts.resolution: Corrected these to string or integer according to their stated semantics.

conflicts.description: Fields described as containing date and time are typed as date in the source schemas.
conflicts.resolution: Canonical event timestamps use datetime.

conflicts.description: The Synthea encounter provider column is documented as an organization foreign key, whereas OMOP provider_id identifies a clinician and care_site_id identifies a facility.
conflicts.resolution: Mapped the Synthea attribute to canonical care_site_id and kept clinician provider_id semantically separate.

conflicts.description: Synthea stores source vocabulary codes directly, while OMOP distinguishes standardized concept identifiers from verbatim source codes.
conflicts.resolution: Kept source_code, source_concept_id, and standardized concept_id fields distinct across clinical domains.

conflicts.description: Source unit strings and standardized unit concepts are different representations, and source units may not be SI.
conflicts.resolution: Retained verbatim unit_source_value separately from unit_concept_id and specified normalized numeric values should use the standardized, preferably SI, unit.

conflicts.description: The term cost is semantically ambiguous in Synthea, while OMOP differentiates charges, provider costs, and payments.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved Synthea values as base_or_line_item_amount and maintained OMOP financial categories as separate attributes.

conflicts.description: Synthea uses compact source encodings such as M/F while OMOP distinguishes source values from standardized concepts.
conflicts.resolution: Retained source encodings in gender_source_value and kept standardized concept identifiers separate.

conflicts.description: Synthea repeats address attributes in entity tables, while OMOP normalizes geographic data into location.
conflicts.resolution: Adopted a normalized location resource and linked persons and care sites through foreign keys; Synthea-derived location identifiers are generated where needed.

conflicts.description: Synthea combines laboratory measurements and other observations in one table, whereas OMOP separates them by clinical domain.
conflicts.resolution: Retained separate measurement and observation resources so numeric measurements and non-measurement clinical assertions remain semantically homogeneous.

conflicts.description: Synthea has one encounter level, while OMOP supports a parent visit plus nested visit details.
conflicts.resolution: Used encounter for the high-level visit and encounter_detail as a normalized child resource.

conflicts.description: Synthea embeds event descriptions while OMOP generally resolves standardized names through concept references.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved source event descriptions and separately retained normalized vocabulary concepts rather than conflating event text with concept master data.

conflicts.description: Synthea contains explicit domain tables without exact one-to-one OMOP counterparts in the supplied schema.
conflicts.resolution: Retained these as independent normalized target resources instead of forcing them into semantically broader OMOP tables.

conflicts.description: A Synthea encounter is a single record, while an OMOP visit occurrence may have one-to-many visit-detail children and nested detail relationships.
conflicts.resolution: Modeled one encounter to many encounter_detail records, with optional self-references for parent and preceding details.

conflicts.description: Synthea embeds one current address per person record, while OMOP allows a normalized location to be referenced by many persons or organizations.
conflicts.resolution: Modeled location as a reusable parent entity referenced by person and care_site.

conflicts.description: Cohort membership is polymorphic: a cohort can contain persons, providers, or visits, and each subject can belong to many cohorts and periods.
conflicts.resolution: Retained cohort membership as an associative resource keyed by definition, subject, and start date, with subject domain declared by the cohort definition.

conflicts.description: Concepts participate in many-to-many directional relationships.
conflicts.resolution: Retained an explicit concept_relationship bridge with source concept, target concept, and relationship type as its composite key.

conflicts.description: Equivalent person entities use differently named source primary keys.
conflicts.resolution: Unified them under person.person_id and included both source primary keys in provenance.

conflicts.description: Equivalent encounter entities use differently named primary keys.
conflicts.resolution: Unified them under encounter.encounter_id and included both source identifiers in provenance.

conflicts.description: Multiple Synthea event tables declare no primary key, whereas OMOP supplies event identifiers, though some are not formally declared as source primary keys.
conflicts.resolution: Canonical event resources use required identifiers; OMOP identifiers are preserved where present and synthetic identifiers are generated only for source rows without explicit event identifiers.

conflicts.description: Synthea describes foreign-key semantics but declares no foreignKeys, while OMOP explicitly declares most relationships.
conflicts.resolution: Declared canonical foreign keys for persons, encounters, providers, care sites, concepts, and normalized child resources.

conflicts.description: Several OMOP associative or definition tables lack declared primary keys despite having identifiable natural or documented unique keys.
conflicts.resolution: Introduced composite keys for cohort membership and concept relationships and a documented identifier key for cohort definitions.

conflicts.description: Patient entity is named 'patients' in Synthea and 'person' in OMOP. Synthea uses plural table names while OMOP uses singular.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized to 'person' (singular) as it aligns with OMOP's convention and common healthcare data model terminology (e.g., FHIR).

conflicts.description: Organization entity is named 'organizations' in Synthea and 'care_site' in OMOP. The terminology differs significantly between schemas.
conflicts.resolution: Adopted 'organization' as the table name since 'care_site' is OMOP-specific terminology, while 'organization' is more generic and matches Synthea's intent.

conflicts.description: Provider entity uses plural 'providers' in Synthea versus singular 'provider' in OMOP.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized to singular 'provider' following common naming conventions for entity tables.

conflicts.description: Encounter entity is a single table 'encounters' in Synthea, while OMOP splits it into hierarchical 'visit_occurrence' (parent) and 'visit_detail' (child) tables.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved OMOP's hierarchical structure with 'visit_occurrence' as the primary encounter table and 'visit_detail' as its child. Synthea encounters are mapped to visit_occurrence.

conflicts.description: Condition entity is named 'conditions' in Synthea and 'condition_occurrence' in OMOP.
conflicts.resolution: Adopted 'condition_occurrence' to align with OMOP's standardized terminology which explicitly indicates the occurrence nature of the record.

conflicts.description: Medication entity is named 'medications' in Synthea and 'drug_exposure' in OMOP, reflecting different scopes (prescriptions vs. all drug exposures).
conflicts.resolution: Used 'drug_exposure' as it encompasses both prescriptions and administrations, providing broader coverage and aligning with OMOP.

conflicts.description: Procedure entity is named 'procedures' in Synthea and 'procedure_occurrence' in OMOP.
conflicts.resolution: Adopted 'procedure_occurrence' to maintain consistency with OMOP's naming pattern for clinical event tables.

conflicts.description: Observation entity exists as a single 'observations' table in Synthea, while OMOP separates it into 'observation' and 'measurement' tables.
conflicts.resolution: Combined into a single 'observation' table with type differentiation via observation_type_concept_id, simplifying the structure while preserving semantic distinctions.

conflicts.description: Synthea uses column names with spaces (e.g., 'body site code') which are invalid in standard SQL and snake_case conventions.
conflicts.resolution: Converted all column names to snake_case (e.g., 'body_site_code', 'body_site_description') to comply with naming standards.

conflicts.description: Cost values are stored as strings in Synthea, preventing numeric operations and comparisons. OMOP uses numeric fields for cost data.
conflicts.resolution: Changed all cost fields to number type to enable mathematical operations, aggregation, and standardization with OMOP's numeric cost representation.

conflicts.description: Temporal fields are inconsistently typed as date or datetime across schemas. Synthea primarily uses date, while OMOP provides both date and datetime fields.
conflicts.resolution: Provided both date and datetime fields where available. Date fields store only the date component, while datetime fields store full timestamp, allowing flexibility in querying.

conflicts.description: Gender is stored as simple string codes ('m'/'f') in Synthea versus concept_id references in OMOP, representing fundamentally different data types.
conflicts.resolution: Included both representations: gender (string) for simple code access and gender_concept_id (string) for standardized concept-based analysis, supporting both use cases.

conflicts.description: Synthea's observations.type field uses a numeric code to indicate data type (text or numeric), while OMOP separates values into distinct typed fields.
conflicts.resolution: Omitted the numeric type indicator in favor of OMOP's approach with separate value_as_number, value_as_string, and value_as_concept_id fields, which provides better type safety.

conflicts.description: Latitude and longitude are stored as strings in OMOP, but should be numeric for geographic calculations.
conflicts.resolution: Changed to number type to enable geographic calculations and validations (latitude: -90 to 90, longitude: -180 to 180).

conflicts.description: Fields that should be numeric (year of birth, utilization count) are stored as strings in source schemas.
conflicts.resolution: Converted to appropriate numeric types (integer for year_of_birth, integer for utilization) to enable proper sorting and calculations.

conflicts.description: Synthea uses direct SNOMED-CT codes for conditions, while OMOP requires mapping to standardized concept identifiers in its vocabulary system.
conflicts.resolution: Implemented a concept table with source_value fields to preserve original codes (condition_source_value) while enabling standardized analysis through concept_id fields.

conflicts.description: Units of measurement are stored as free text in Synthea (e.g., 'mg/dL'), while OMOP uses standardized unit concept identifiers.
conflicts.resolution: Used unit_concept_id for standardized units with unit_source_value to preserve original unit strings, enabling both standardized and source-specific analysis.

conflicts.description: Synthea stores address as a single string field, while OMOP splits it into address_1 (street) and address_2 (apartment/suite) for better normalization.
conflicts.resolution: Adopted OMOP's split address fields in the location table, mapping Synthea's single address field to address_1.

conflicts.description: Medication codes in Synthea use RxNorm directly, while OMOP requires mapping to its standardized drug concepts.
conflicts.resolution: Used drug_concept_id for standardized references with drug_source_value to preserve original RxNorm codes from Synthea.

conflicts.description: Synthea's imaging study body site codes use SNOMED-CT directly, while OMOP requires concept-based references.
conflicts.resolution: Mapped to body_site_concept_id with body_site_source_value preserving the original SNOMED-CT codes.

conflicts.description: OMOP includes extensive vocabulary metadata tables (concept, domain, vocabulary, etc.) that enable standardized coding across all clinical data, while Synthea has no equivalent normalization.
conflicts.resolution: Included the full OMOP vocabulary table structure to support standardized coding, concept hierarchies, and cross-walking between coding systems.

conflicts.description: OMOP models visits hierarchically with visit_occurrence as parent and visit_detail as child (1:N relationship), while Synthea has a flat encounter structure.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved OMOP's hierarchical structure with visit_detail referencing visit_occurrence. Synthea encounters are mapped to visit_occurrence, with no direct equivalent for visit_detail.

conflicts.description: OMOP systematically stores original source codes in _source_value fields alongside standardized concept_ids, while Synthea only has direct code fields.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized on the OMOP pattern: every concept_id field has a corresponding _source_value field to preserve original codes, with Synthea's code fields mapped to _source_value.

conflicts.description: Synthea stores encounter start/stop as date only, while OMOP provides separate date and datetime fields for temporal precision.
conflicts.resolution: Provided both date and datetime fields in visit_occurrence to accommodate both precision levels, with date fields populated from either source.

conflicts.description: Several Synthea tables (careplans, allergies, medications, etc.) lack defined primary keys, using composite keys implicitly instead.
conflicts.resolution: Introduced explicit surrogate primary keys (e.g., care_plan_id, allergy_id) for all tables to ensure each record has a unique identifier, with source_provenance: [] for synthetic keys.

conflicts.description: Synthea encounters reference organizations via the provider field (foreign key to organizations.id), while OMOP visit_occurrence references individual providers via provider_id (foreign key to provider table).
conflicts.resolution: Added both provider_id (individual) and organization_id fields to visit_occurrence to support both models: individual provider tracking (OMOP) and organization-level provider attribution (Synthea).

conflicts.description: Synthea conditions reference encounters directly, while OMOP condition_occurrence can reference both visit_occurrence and visit_detail, enabling more granular association.
conflicts.resolution: Included both visit_occurrence_id and visit_detail_id in condition_occurrence to support OMOP's more granular visit hierarchy, with Synthea's encounter mapping to visit_occurrence_id.

conflicts.description: OMOP drug_exposure can be associated with either visit_occurrence or visit_detail, while Synthea medications only reference encounters (visit_occurrence equivalent).
conflicts.resolution: Maintained both visit_occurrence_id and visit_detail_id foreign keys in drug_exposure to preserve OMOP's flexibility, with Synthea's encounter field mapping to visit_occurrence_id.

conflicts.description: Synthea uses 'id' as the primary key field name for entities, while OMOP uses '_id' suffix (e.g., person_id, visit_occurrence_id).
conflicts.resolution: Standardized all primary keys to use '_id' suffix (e.g., person_id, visit_occurrence_id) for consistency across the unified schema.

conflicts.description: Many Synthea tables (conditions, allergies, medications, etc.) have no defined primary key, relying on implicit composite keys of patient + encounter + code.
conflicts.resolution: Introduced explicit primary keys for all tables (e.g., condition_occurrence_id, allergy_id) to ensure each record has a unique identifier, with source_provenance: [] for synthetic keys that have no source counterpart.

conflicts.description: Synthea uses simple field names for foreign keys (e.g., 'patient' in encounters), while OMOP uses '_id' suffix for all foreign keys (e.g., person_id).
conflicts.resolution: Standardized all foreign key fields to use '_id' suffix (e.g., person_id, visit_occurrence_id) for consistency, with appropriate mappings from source fields.

conflicts.description: Different table names for the same semantic entity representing individuals. Synthea uses 'patients' while OMOP uses 'person'.
conflicts.resolution: Adopted OMOP's 'person' as the standard table name as it's more precise and aligns with healthcare data modeling conventions.

conflicts.description: Different naming for visit/encounter entities. Synthea has a single 'encounters' table while OMOP has 'visit_occurrence' and 'visit_detail' tables.
conflicts.resolution: Used OMOP's 'visit_occurrence' and 'visit_detail' tables to maintain the hierarchical visit structure, mapping Synthea encounters to visit_occurrence.

conflicts.description: Different naming conventions for condition records. Synthea uses 'conditions' while OMOP uses 'condition_occurrence'.
conflicts.resolution: Adopted OMOP's 'condition_occurrence' naming as it better reflects the event-based nature of the data.

conflicts.description: Different naming for medication records. Synthea uses 'medications' while OMOP uses 'drug_exposure'.
conflicts.resolution: Used OMOP's 'drug_exposure' as the primary table name, incorporating medication data from Synthea.

conflicts.description: Synthea has a dedicated 'allergies' table which has no direct equivalent in OMOP. OMOP typically represents allergies as conditions or observations.
conflicts.resolution: Created new 'allergy' table in the target schema to preserve this important clinical entity.

conflicts.description: Synthea has a single 'observations' table while OMOP splits observations into 'observation' (categorical) and 'measurement' (numeric) tables.
conflicts.resolution: Adopted OMOP's split structure with both 'observation' and 'measurement' tables, mapping Synthea observations based on their type field.

conflicts.description: Synthea has an 'imaging_studies' table with no direct equivalent in OMOP.
conflicts.resolution: Created new 'imaging_study' table to preserve this specialized clinical data.

conflicts.description: Synthea has an 'immunizations' table which in OMOP would typically be part of drug_exposure or procedure_occurrence.
conflicts.resolution: Created dedicated 'immunization' table to properly represent this clinical entity.

conflicts.description: Synthea has a single 'organizations' table while OMOP splits into 'care_site' (logical) and 'location' (physical address) tables.
conflicts.resolution: Adopted OMOP's normalized structure with separate 'care_site' and 'location' tables, mapping Synthea organizations to care_site.

conflicts.description: Different field names for provider specialty: Synthea uses 'speciality' while OMOP uses 'specialty' (without the 'i').
conflicts.resolution: Standardized on OMOP's 'specialty' spelling for consistency across the schema.

conflicts.description: Cost is represented as a string in Synthea tables, while OMOP has a dedicated cost table with multiple numeric fields for different cost components.
conflicts.resolution: Included cost as a number type in clinical event tables (drug_exposure, procedure_occurrence, etc.) for line-item costs, and retained the full OMOP cost table for detailed cost breakdowns.

conflicts.description: Synthea uses date-only fields for temporal attributes, while OMOP provides both date and datetime fields for greater precision.
conflicts.resolution: Included both date and datetime fields in temporal attributes across all tables, allowing for maximum precision when available.

conflicts.description: Gender is represented as simple 'm'/'f' codes in Synthea, while OMOP uses standardized concept identifiers from controlled vocabularies.
conflicts.resolution: Used concept_id as the primary gender identifier, with gender_source_value preserving the original source codes from both systems.

conflicts.description: Synthea uses a numeric type field for observations, while OMOP uses concept_id to reference standardized observation type concepts.
conflicts.resolution: Adopted OMOP's concept_id approach, with the numeric type from Synthea being mapped to appropriate concepts during ETL.

conflicts.description: Synthea has a single string value field for observations, while OMOP has separate fields for different value types (number, string, concept).
conflicts.resolution: Implemented OMOP's typed value approach with separate fields, mapping Synthea's value field to the appropriate type based on its observation type.

conflicts.description: Synthea uses direct coding system codes (SNOMED-CT, LOINC, etc.) in various tables, while OMOP standardizes all clinical codes to concept_id from controlled vocabularies.
conflicts.resolution: Used concept_id as the primary identifier for all clinical entities, with source code fields preserved to maintain traceability to original coding systems.

conflicts.description: Synthea represents units of measure as strings, while OMOP uses standardized unit concept identifiers from controlled vocabularies.
conflicts.resolution: Implemented unit_concept_id as the primary unit identifier, with unit_source_value preserving the original string representations.

conflicts.description: Synthea has address fields embedded directly in patient, organization, and provider tables, while OMOP uses a separate location table for all address information.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized all address information into a single location table, with foreign key references from person, care_site, and provider tables.

conflicts.description: Synthea includes utilization metrics (counts of encounters) in organizations and providers, which are not present in OMOP.
conflicts.resolution: Added utilization fields to both care_site and provider tables to preserve this operational metric from Synthea.

conflicts.description: Gender values use different coding schemes: Synthea uses 'm'/'f' while OMOP source values may use different codes depending on the source system.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized on gender_concept_id for analysis while preserving source values, with proper mapping between systems during ETL.

conflicts.description: Synthea has a relatively denormalized structure with repeated fields and embedded data, while OMOP is highly normalized with extensive use of foreign keys to controlled vocabulary tables.
conflicts.resolution: Adopted OMOP's normalized structure as the foundation, which provides better data integrity and supports more sophisticated analytics.

conflicts.description: Synthea has a flat encounters table, while OMOP implements a hierarchical visit model with visit_occurrence as parent and visit_detail as child.
conflicts.resolution: Maintained OMOP's hierarchical visit structure to support detailed visit analysis while mapping Synthea encounters to the visit_occurrence level.

conflicts.description: OMOP includes era tables (condition_era, drug_era, dose_era) that represent continuous periods of conditions or drug exposure, which are derived from the underlying occurrence tables. Synthea does not have equivalent structures.
conflicts.resolution: Included all era tables in the target schema as they provide valuable temporal abstraction for analytical queries.

conflicts.description: OMOP has a comprehensive vocabulary and metadata layer with concept, vocabulary, domain, and relationship tables that enable standardized analytics across different source systems. Synthea lacks this infrastructure.
conflicts.resolution: Included the full OMOP vocabulary infrastructure in the target schema to enable standardized, cross-system analytics.

conflicts.description: Synthea includes specialized clinical tables (imaging_studies, immunizations, allergies) that don't have direct equivalents in OMOP's core schema.
conflicts.resolution: Created dedicated tables for these entities in the target schema to preserve the full breadth of clinical data from Synthea.

conflicts.description: Synthea references encounters directly from clinical event tables, while OMOP uses both visit_occurrence_id and visit_detail_id to provide more precise visit context for clinical events.
conflicts.resolution: Implemented both visit_occurrence_id and visit_detail_id as foreign keys in all clinical event tables to support both coarse and fine-grained visit associations.

conflicts.description: Synthea does not explicitly link patients to providers or organizations, while OMOP includes provider_id and care_site_id in the person table to indicate primary care relationships.
conflicts.resolution: Included provider_id and care_site_id in the person table to capture primary care relationships, populating from OMOP and leaving null for Synthea data where not available.

conflicts.description: Synthea uses generic 'id' field names for primary keys, while OMOP uses descriptive names like person_id, visit_occurrence_id that indicate the entity type.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized on OMOP's descriptive primary key naming convention throughout the schema for clarity and consistency.

conflicts.description: Synthea uses field names like 'patient' and 'encounter' for foreign keys, while OMOP uses the standard entity name with '_id' suffix (person_id, visit_occurrence_id).
conflicts.resolution: Adopted OMOP's naming convention for all foreign keys (e.g., person_id instead of patient, visit_occurrence_id instead of encounter) to maintain consistency across the schema.

conflicts.description: Synthea uses 'organization' as the foreign key to link providers to organizations, while OMOP uses 'care_site_id' to link to the care_site table.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized on care_site_id as the foreign key, mapping Synthea's organization field to care_site_id during ETL.

conflicts.description: The core person entity is named 'patients' in Synthea and 'person' in OMOP.
conflicts.resolution: Unified into target resource 'patient' (snake_case, singular).

conflicts.description: The clinical interaction entity is 'encounters' in Synthea and 'visit_occurrence' in OMOP.
conflicts.resolution: Unified into target resource 'encounter'; related sub-entity visit_detail mapped to 'encounter_detail'.

conflicts.description: Facility/location-of-care entity named 'organizations' vs 'care_site'.
conflicts.resolution: Unified into target resource 'organization'; OMOP care_site identifiers retained as care_site_* columns/FKs.

conflicts.description: Medication fact named 'medications' vs 'drug_exposure'.
conflicts.resolution: Unified into target resource 'medication'.

conflicts.description: Procedure fact named 'procedures' vs 'procedure_occurrence'.
conflicts.resolution: Unified into target resource 'procedure'.

conflicts.description: Condition fact named 'conditions' vs 'condition_occurrence'.
conflicts.resolution: Unified into target resource 'condition'.

conflicts.description: Synthea 'observations' overlaps both OMOP 'observation' and 'measurement'.
conflicts.resolution: Unified into a single target resource 'observation' capturing textual and numeric results.

conflicts.description: Clinician entity uses plural 'providers' vs singular 'provider'.
conflicts.resolution: Unified into target resource 'provider'.

conflicts.description: Identifier naming differs: Synthea uses bare 'id', OMOP uses '<entity>_id'.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized to snake_case '<entity>_id' surrogate naming across all target tables.

conflicts.description: Synthea imaging_studies columns contain spaces and are not snake_case.
conflicts.resolution: Renamed to snake_case (body_site_code, modality_code, sop_code, etc.).

conflicts.description: Spelling inconsistency: 'speciality' (Synthea) vs 'specialty' (OMOP).
conflicts.resolution: Standardized on 'specialty'-based naming; kept Synthea verbatim value in 'speciality'.

conflicts.description: Column named 'provider' is described as a foreign key to the organization, conflicting with provider semantics.
conflicts.resolution: Resolved as a provider (clinician) foreign key and merged with omop.visit_occurrence.provider_id, aligned with naming.

conflicts.description: Monetary cost fields are stored as 'string' in Synthea but are numeric quantities.
conflicts.resolution: Cast to 'number' in target (cost).

conflicts.description: OMOP types the birth-date components as 'date', though they are integer calendar components.
conflicts.resolution: Retyped to 'integer' (birth_year, birth_month, birth_day).

conflicts.description: Coordinates typed as 'string' though they are numeric.
conflicts.resolution: Retyped to 'number'.

conflicts.description: Reference-range bounds typed as 'string' though numeric.
conflicts.resolution: Retyped to 'number'.

conflicts.description: Quantity fields typed as 'string' though numeric.
conflicts.resolution: Retyped to 'number'.

conflicts.description: Primary key typed as 'date' instead of an identifier.
conflicts.resolution: Retyped to 'string'.

conflicts.description: Vocabulary name typed as 'integer' though it is text.
conflicts.resolution: Retyped to 'string'.

conflicts.description: Concept identifier typed as 'number' while all sibling concept ids are 'string'.
conflicts.resolution: Retyped to 'string' for consistency.

conflicts.description: Categorical reason flags (D/U/NULL) typed as 'date'.
conflicts.resolution: Retyped to 'string'.

conflicts.description: Concept/monetary fields inconsistently typed as 'integer' while peers are 'string'/'number'.
conflicts.resolution: currency_concept_id retyped to 'string'; paid_patient_coinsurance retyped to 'number'.

conflicts.description: Field described as a datatype indicator (text/numeric) but typed as 'number'.
conflicts.resolution: Retyped to 'string' (value_type).

conflicts.description: Boolean flag fields typed as 'integer'/'string' with values 1/0.
conflicts.resolution: Retyped to 'boolean'.

conflicts.description: Concatenated modifier string typed as 'integer'.
conflicts.resolution: Retyped to 'string'.

conflicts.description: Source coding fields typed as 'integer' though codes may be alphanumeric.
conflicts.resolution: Retyped to 'string'.

conflicts.description: Gender encoded as single letters ('m'/'f') in Synthea vs a standardized gender Concept plus verbatim source value in OMOP.
conflicts.resolution: Retained 'gender' (verbatim Synthea code) alongside 'gender_concept_id'/'gender_source_value'; scale normalization handled via the concept vocabulary.

conflicts.description: Race/ethnicity are free-text descriptions in Synthea vs standardized multi-column concept+source representations in OMOP.
conflicts.resolution: Kept Synthea description columns and OMOP concept/source columns side by side; standardized values expressible via the concept table.

conflicts.description: Units are free text in Synthea vs a coded unit concept + verbatim source in OMOP.
conflicts.resolution: Unified to 'unit_source_value' (verbatim, all sources) plus 'unit_concept_id' (standardized); standard SI units promoted through the concept mapping.

conflicts.description: OMOP monetary values carry an explicit currency concept; Synthea costs carry no currency information.
conflicts.resolution: Cost amounts kept numeric; currency only available through the OMOP cost table, documented as a semantic gap for Synthea-sourced costs.

conflicts.description: Synthea stores native vocabulary codes (SNOMED-CT, RxNorm, LOINC, CVX); OMOP stores both a source value and a mapped standard Concept id.
conflicts.resolution: Synthea codes mapped to '*_source_value' columns and harmonized with OMOP source values; standardized meaning via '*_concept_id'.

conflicts.description: Marital status uses single-letter codes (m/s) with limited coverage (no d/w).
conflicts.resolution: Retained verbatim as 'marital_status' string; no OMOP counterpart column, left as source-specific attribute.

conflicts.description: Temporal granularity differs: Synthea keeps date only; OMOP keeps parallel date and datetime columns.
conflicts.resolution: Both granularities preserved with distinct '*_date'/'*_datetime' columns.

conflicts.description: Synthea denormalizes address attributes into patient/provider/organization rows, whereas OMOP normalizes them into a separate LOCATION table referenced by FK.
conflicts.resolution: Introduced a normalized 'location' resource for OMOP geometry; Synthea address attributes retained as denormalized columns on their owner entities to preserve column-level provenance.

conflicts.description: OMOP uses a paired concept/source representation for coded attributes; Synthea uses a single code+description pair.
conflicts.resolution: Both representations coexisted per attribute (concept_id + source_value + verbatim description) rather than collapsing them.

conflicts.description: OMOP splits observation-type facts and numeric lab measurements into separate tables; Synthea holds them in one table with a value/units/type triple.
conflicts.resolution: Decomposed/normalized into a single unified 'observation' table that captures both textual (value_as_string) and numeric (value_as_number) results.

conflicts.description: Synthea keeps a single full birth date; OMOP keeps a datetime plus extracted year/month/day components.
conflicts.resolution: Kept 'birth_date' plus explicit birth_year/month/day integer components in the unified patient table.

conflicts.description: Synthea models a single encounter; OMOP decomposes visits into visit_occurrence plus a child visit_detail hierarchy.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved both levels as 'encounter' and 'encounter_detail' with a parent-child FK between them.

conflicts.description: Synthea stores death as a single patient attribute; OMOP models a separate 1:1 DEATH table with cause/type concepts.
conflicts.resolution: Folded the 1:1 death record into the 'patient' resource (death_date/datetime, cause and type concepts).

conflicts.description: Synthea imaging studies have no dedicated OMOP table and overlap loosely with procedure/measurement facts.
conflicts.resolution: Retained as a standalone 'imaging_study' resource to avoid lossy forcing into procedure/observation.

conflicts.description: OMOP defines a 1:N relationship between visit_occurrence and visit_detail; Synthea's encounter has no such nesting.
conflicts.resolution: Modeled as encounter (1) to encounter_detail (N) via encounter_id FK; Synthea encounters populate only the parent level.

conflicts.description: Synthea conditions are event-level (1 row per event) while OMOP additionally aggregates events into condition eras (1:N events per era).
conflicts.resolution: Event-level 'condition' retained as canonical; aggregated era structures left to be derived and not conflated with event rows.

conflicts.description: Both describe a many-to-one relationship between providers and the organization/care site they belong to.
conflicts.resolution: Merged both provider-to-organization references into a single 'care_site_id' FK to the 'organization' resource.

conflicts.description: OMOP links a person to a primary care provider (1:1 attribute); Synthea has no such patient-provider link.
conflicts.resolution: Retained patient.provider_id (nullable) sourced only from OMOP; no Synthea provenance.

conflicts.description: OMOP defines one-to-many person-to-coverage and person-to-observation-period relationships that Synthea lacks.
conflicts.resolution: Modeled as separate child resources (payer_plan_period, observation_period) keyed to patient.

conflicts.description: Several Synthea tables (allergies, conditions, medications, procedures, observations, immunizations) declare no primary key.
conflicts.resolution: OMOP surrogate keys adopted where available; purely synthetic surrogate keys (e.g., allergy_id, immunization_id) introduced only for target mechanics and marked with empty provenance.

conflicts.description: Primary key identification differs: Synthea relies on a generic 'id' while OMOP uses explicit entity-scoped keys, and some OMOP keys were mistyped.
conflicts.resolution: Harmonized to a single snake_case '<entity>_id' key per unified resource, with both source keys listed in provenance.

conflicts.description: Synthea's encounter 'provider' column ambiguously references an organization, whereas OMOP separates provider_id and care_site_id foreign keys.
conflicts.resolution: Resolved as a provider clinician FK (provider_id) and retained a distinct care_site_id FK to organization.

conflicts.description: Synthea expresses foreign keys as bare columns (patient, encounter) with no declared key relationships.
conflicts.resolution: Reconstructed explicit foreign keys (patient_id, encounter_id, provider_id) referencing the unified parent resources.

conflicts.description: payer_plan_period_id was declared with a non-identifier type, weakening key identification.
conflicts.resolution: Retyped to 'string' and promoted to the primary key of 'payer_plan_period'.

conflicts.description: OMOP uses polymorphic 'event_id' + '*_event_field_concept_id' keys whose target entity is data-dependent.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved as generic event id plus field concept id (not resolvable as a static FK), documented as a polymorphic relationship.

fields.description: Datatype of the recorded value (text or numeric).

conflicts.description: The same real-world entity (an individual receiving care) is named 'patients' in Synthea and 'person' in OMOP.
conflicts.resolution: Unified into a single target resource 'patient'; the identification attribute is normalized to 'patient_id'.

conflicts.description: Synthea calls the care-contact event 'encounters', while OMOP names it 'visit_occurrence' and additionally introduces a nested 'visit_detail'.
conflicts.resolution: Unified into target 'encounter' with encounter_id; the OMOP visit_detail level is treated as a structural sub-detail conflict (see Structure).

conflicts.description: Synthea table 'conditions' corresponds to OMOP 'condition_occurrence'.
conflicts.resolution: Unified into target 'condition_occurrence'.

conflicts.description: Synthea 'medications' corresponds to OMOP 'drug_exposure'.
conflicts.resolution: Unified into target 'drug_exposure'.

conflicts.description: Synthea 'procedures' corresponds to OMOP 'procedure_occurrence'.
conflicts.resolution: Unified into target 'procedure_occurrence'.

conflicts.description: Synthea 'organizations' corresponds to OMOP 'care_site'.
conflicts.resolution: Unified into target 'organization' with organization_id.

conflicts.description: Misspelled column name 'speciality' in Synthea versus correctly spelled 'specialty' in OMOP.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized spelling to 'specialty_source_value' / 'specialty_concept_id'.

conflicts.description: Synthea imaging_studies uses column names containing spaces and non-snake_case naming.
conflicts.resolution: All column names converted to snake_case (e.g. 'body site code' -> body_site_code; 'date' -> study_date to avoid a reserved/generic name).

conflicts.description: Homonym conflict: the Synthea 'provider' column in encounters is documented as a foreign key to the organization, not to a clinician, clashing with the general meaning of 'provider'.
conflicts.resolution: Mapped to care_site_id referencing the organization entity; clinician-level reference retained separately as provider_id from OMOP.

conflicts.description: Synthea 'observations' overlaps both OMOP 'observation' and OMOP 'measurement', which are distinct named entities.
conflicts.resolution: Synthea observations merged into target 'observation'; OMOP 'measurement' retained as its own target resource to preserve key distinctness (see Structure/Key).

conflicts.description: Synthea monetary cost fields are typed as string but represent numeric monetary amounts.
conflicts.resolution: Retyped to number in the target (base_cost, cost).

conflicts.description: OMOP birth component fields are declared as 'date' but semantically hold integer calendar components.
conflicts.resolution: Retyped to integer; full birth moment consolidated into birth_date.

conflicts.description: Geographic coordinates declared as string but are numeric quantities.
conflicts.resolution: Retyped to number.

conflicts.description: vocabulary_name is declared as integer but holds descriptive text.
conflicts.resolution: Retyped to string.

conflicts.description: Identifier column declared as 'date' although it is a surrogate identifier.
conflicts.resolution: Treated as string identifier (out of unified core; flagged for correction).

conflicts.description: The invalid_reason code attribute is declared as 'date' in several OMOP tables but holds alphabetic codes (D/U).
conflicts.resolution: Retyped to string in the target concept resource.

conflicts.description: Synthea describes encounter start/stop as date-and-time but types them as 'date'; OMOP supplies separate date and datetime columns.
conflicts.resolution: Split into start_date/end_date (date) and start_datetime/end_datetime (datetime) in the target encounter.

conflicts.description: term_modifiers declared as integer but semantically carries concatenated textual modifiers.
conflicts.resolution: Retyped to string (out of unified core; flagged for correction).

conflicts.description: Concept identifier columns are inconsistently typed as integer or number across OMOP tables vs string elsewhere.
conflicts.resolution: All concept identifiers standardized to string.

conflicts.description: Synthea encodes gender as single letters (m/f); OMOP uses vocabulary concept identifiers plus a verbatim source value.
conflicts.resolution: Both representations retained: gender_source_value holds Synthea's letter and OMOP's source value, gender_concept_id holds the OMOP standard concept.

conflicts.description: Synthea stores race/ethnicity as free-text descriptions, whereas OMOP uses coded concept identifiers.
conflicts.resolution: Separated into *_source_value (verbatim text) and *_concept_id (standardized code) columns.

conflicts.description: Synthea keeps clinical codes inline using domain-specific vocabularies (SNOMED-CT, RxNorm, LOINC, CVX, DICOM); OMOP centralizes codes in the CONCEPT vocabulary with concept identifiers.
conflicts.resolution: Source codes preserved as *_source_value; standardized mapping retained through *_concept_id referencing the shared concept resource.

conflicts.description: Units of measure are free text in Synthea but coded concepts in OMOP; representational scale differs.
conflicts.resolution: unit_source_value preserves the verbatim unit and unit_concept_id preserves the coded unit; both retained.

conflicts.description: Synthea's single base 'cost' field conflates several semantically distinct monetary measures that OMOP separates (charge, incurred cost, amounts paid).
conflicts.resolution: Synthea encounters.cost mapped to base_cost; distinct OMOP monetary semantics kept separate rather than merged.

conflicts.description: Encounter class is an enumerated string in Synthea (ambulatory, emergency...) while OMOP uses a visit concept identifier.
conflicts.resolution: encounter_class preserves the Synthea category string; encounter_concept_id preserves the OMOP coded visit type.

conflicts.description: Synthea uses compact single-letter codes (m/s for marital status) whose semantics are non-obvious.
conflicts.resolution: Values retained verbatim in marital_status; categorical encoding documented as a semantic resolution concern.

conflicts.description: Synthea embeds address attributes (street/city/state/zip) directly in each entity; OMOP normalizes them into a separate LOCATION resource referenced by foreign key.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized into a reusable target 'location' resource with location_id foreign keys from patient/organization; Synthea inline address columns retained on patient/organization for lossless capture.

conflicts.description: OMOP fully normalizes a terminology/vocabulary subsystem; Synthea keeps inline codes with no such reference layer.
conflicts.resolution: Core 'concept' resource retained as the shared coding reference; deeper vocabulary tables treated as an OMOP-only subsystem to be materialized alongside.

conflicts.description: Synthea collapses all observation results into a single typed-union value column plus a value_type marker; OMOP splits results across value_as_number/value_as_string/value_as_concept_id.
conflicts.resolution: Value disaggregated into value_as_number, value_as_string and value_as_concept_id; Synthea value_type preserved as a discriminator column.

conflicts.description: OMOP decomposes a visit into a parent visit_occurrence and a nested visit_detail, whereas Synthea has a single flat encounter level.
conflicts.resolution: Flat 'encounter' resource retained as the unified parent; visit_detail_id columns preserved on event tables for OMOP lineage.

conflicts.description: Synthea models death as an attribute (deathdate) on the patient, while OMOP models it as a separate DEATH resource with cause and type.
conflicts.resolution: Death retained as a dedicated target 'death' resource keyed by patient_id; the plain death_date is also projected onto the patient for the Synthea view.

conflicts.description: Synthea holds line-item costs inline on each event; OMOP normalizes all costs into a polymorphic COST resource.
conflicts.resolution: Synthea inline costs retained on each event (base_cost/cost); the normalized OMOP COST resource is recognized as a separate structural representation of the same measures.

conflicts.description: Both schemas model one patient to many encounters/events, but this 1:N relationship is only implicitly expressed in Synthea via foreign-key columns.
conflicts.resolution: 1:N preserved with patient_id foreign keys on all event resources.

conflicts.description: Provider-to-organization membership is 1:N from organization to provider in both schemas, but Synthea expresses it as a plain FK column without a declared relationship.
conflicts.resolution: care_site_id foreign key on provider referencing organization.

conflicts.description: OMOP contains self-referential and bridge tables expressing many-to-many hierarchies (concept ancestry, concept/relationship, episode-event), with no Synthea counterpart.
conflicts.resolution: Recognized as OMOP-only N:M structures; retained as separate bridge resources outside the merged core entities.

conflicts.description: OMOP imposes a strict 1:N parent-child cardinality between visit_occurrence and visit_detail; Synthea has no equivalent nesting level.
conflicts.resolution: Modeled as encounter (parent) to nested visit_detail children via visit_detail_id on event tables.

conflicts.description: OMOP links person and care_site to a shared location (reused N:1), while Synthea stores a distinct inline address per row with no sharing.
conflicts.resolution: Location normalized to a shared 1:N reference so multiple entities can point to one location_id.

conflicts.description: Synthea child tables declare no primary key at all, whereas their OMOP counterparts expose explicit surrogate identifiers.
conflicts.resolution: Target primary keys drawn from the OMOP identifiers where available; purely synthetic surrogate keys (immunization_id, allergy_id) introduced where no source key exists.

conflicts.description: Primary key identification conflict: the patient identifier is named 'id' in Synthea and 'person_id' in OMOP.
conflicts.resolution: Unified primary key patient_id with provenance from both.

conflicts.description: Encounter primary key is named 'id' in Synthea and 'visit_occurrence_id' in OMOP.
conflicts.resolution: Unified primary key encounter_id with provenance from both.

conflicts.description: Foreign-key identification difference: Synthea references the organization via a column named 'organization', OMOP via 'care_site_id'.
conflicts.resolution: Both mapped to care_site_id referencing the unified organization key.

conflicts.description: OMOP distinguishes standardized concept keys from source concept keys for the same event, in contrast to Synthea's single inline code.
conflicts.resolution: Both standardized (*_concept_id) and source (*_source_concept_id/*_source_value) keys retained, all ultimately referencing the shared concept resource.

conflicts.description: Synthea conflates provider and organization identity naming (encounters.provider points to organization), risking key confusion between the physician entity and the facility entity.
conflicts.resolution: Separated into distinct care_site_id (organization) and provider_id (clinician) keys; the Synthea encounters.provider column definitively mapped to care_site_id.

target_schema.name: unified_clinical
target_schema.title: Unified Clinical Data Package (Synthea + OMOP CDM)

conflicts.description: The core demographic entity is named 'patients' in synthea but 'person' in OMOP.
conflicts.resolution: Unified to the target resource 'person'; synthea.patients.id and omop.person.person_id are grouped as the target person_id primary key.

conflicts.description: The clinical contact entity is 'encounters' in synthea versus 'visit_occurrence'/'visit_detail' in OMOP.
conflicts.resolution: Merged into the target resource 'encounter'; OMOP's finer-grained visit_detail hierarchy is preserved as a separate child resource.

conflicts.description: The facility entity is 'organizations' in synthea versus 'care_site' in OMOP.
conflicts.resolution: Unified to the target resource 'care_site'.

conflicts.description: Synonym column naming: synthea.providers.name / speciality versus omop.provider.provider_name / specialty_source_value.
conflicts.resolution: Aligned to provider_name and specialty_source_value; misspelling 'speciality' corrected.

conflicts.description: Synonym patterns: synthea uses generic 'code'/'description' while OMOP uses '<domain>_source_value'/'<domain>_concept_id'.
conflicts.resolution: Mapped synthea 'code' to the target '<domain>_code' (aligned to OMOP *_source_value) and synthea 'description' to '<domain>_description'.

conflicts.description: Synonym patterns: synthea uses 'start'/'stop'; OMOP uses '<domain>_start_date'/'<domain>_end_date'.
conflicts.resolution: Aligned synthea start/stop to the target start_date/end_date columns per domain.

conflicts.description: synthea.imaging_studies uses human-readable column names containing spaces; the target requires snake_case.
conflicts.resolution: Renamed to snake_case (body_site_code, sop_code, modality_code, etc.).

conflicts.description: Monetary amounts are typed as string (synthea and OMOP cost) rather than numeric in the sources.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized monetary columns to the Frictionless 'number' type in the target.

conflicts.description: OMOP declares inconsistent types: an identifier typed as date, a name typed as integer, and a concept-id typed as number.
conflicts.resolution: Corrected types in the target: identifiers and concept-ids to string; descriptive names to string.

conflicts.description: synthea.observations.type ('text or numeric') is declared as number although it is a categorical data-type indicator.
conflicts.resolution: Retyped to string in the target.

conflicts.description: OMOP '*_datetime' columns are declared as 'date' although they carry time-of-day precision.
conflicts.resolution: Retyped to the Frictionless 'datetime' type in the target.

conflicts.description: Integer-like counters are typed as string in the sources.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized count/utilization columns to 'integer' in the target.

conflicts.description: synthea encounter start/stop are described as 'date and time' but typed as 'date'.
conflicts.resolution: Retained date precision on start_date/end_date; OMOP datetime variants are carried on dedicated start_datetime/end_datetime columns.

conflicts.description: Gender is encoded as 'm'/'f' in synthea versus source value plus standard concept id in OMOP.
conflicts.resolution: Unified to gender_source_value, with gender_concept_id retained for standardized coding.

conflicts.description: Units are free text in synthea versus source value + standardized unit concept in OMOP.
conflicts.resolution: Unified to unit_source_value; unit_concept_id retained for standardized units.

conflicts.description: synthea stores raw SNOMED-CT/RxNorm/LOINC/CVX codes; OMOP stores the same as *_source_value paired with a mapped *_source_concept_id.
conflicts.resolution: Unified the raw code into '<domain>_code' (equivalent to *_source_value) and kept separate '<domain>_source_concept_id' columns for OMOP mapping.

conflicts.description: synthea stores a single full birth date; OMOP stores a birth datetime plus decomposed year/month/day components.
conflicts.resolution: Birth date unified to birth_date (grouping birthdate and birth_datetime); decomposed OMOP components retained as distinct columns.

conflicts.description: synthea records a single encounter/line-item cost inline; OMOP records detailed, decomposed cost components in a dedicated cost table.
conflicts.resolution: synthea inline cost retained as an event-level 'cost' attribute; OMOP's normalized cost components retained in the 'cost' resource. Flagged as a residual denormalization.

conflicts.description: Encounter class is a free-text categorical (ambulatory/emergency/…) in synthea versus a standardized visit concept in OMOP.
conflicts.resolution: Retained encounter_class as a categorical attribute and visit_concept_id as the standardized counterpart.

conflicts.description: Marital status exists only in synthea with no OMOP equivalent.
conflicts.resolution: Retained as a person-level attribute with provenance restricted to synthea.

conflicts.description: synthea is a flat, denormalized clinical schema; OMOP is a normalized CDM with standardized vocabulary and era tables.
conflicts.resolution: Adopted the normalized OMOP-style structure as the global skeleton, absorbing synthea attributes into the analogous entities.

conflicts.description: Addresses are embedded inline in synthea entities but normalized into a shared location resource referenced by FK in OMOP.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized all addresses into the 'location' resource; person, care_site and provider reference it via location_id.

conflicts.description: synthea carries inline reasoncode/reasondescription pairs; OMOP expresses reasons through standardized concept foreign keys.
conflicts.resolution: Retained synthea reason_code/reason_description as source attributes; OMOP concept columns preserved separately.

conflicts.description: Era (aggregated time-span) entities exist only in OMOP with no synthea counterpart.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved as dedicated target resources (condition_era, drug_era, dose_era).

conflicts.description: OMOP's standardized vocabulary/reference tables have no synthea counterpart.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved as standalone target resources retaining their native structure and FKs.

conflicts.description: synthea has clinical event tables (immunizations, allergies, imaging studies, care plans) with no directly named OMOP entity.
conflicts.resolution: Retained as dedicated target resources (immunization, allergy, imaging_study, care_plan) rather than forcing lossy remapping.

conflicts.description: OMOP models a two-level visit hierarchy (visit_occurrence → visit_detail) while synthea exposes a single flat encounter table.
conflicts.resolution: Encounter unified to encounter; the visit_detail child level retained as a separate resource referenced by encounter.

conflicts.description: synthea encounters are a flat 1-level list; OMOP defines a 1:N parent/child relationship between visit_occurrence and visit_detail.
conflicts.resolution: Modeled encounter as the parent and visit_detail as a 1:N child via visit_occurrence_id FK.

conflicts.description: OMOP episode nests sub-episodes (self-reference) and links to events 1:N via episode_event; synthea has no equivalent.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved episode (with episode_parent_id self-reference) and episode_event bridge as separate resources.

conflicts.description: Death is 1:1 with the person; synthea encodes it inline (deathdate) while OMOP uses a separate death table keyed by person_id.
conflicts.resolution: Modeled death as a separate 1:1 resource keyed by person_id; synthea deathdate mapped to death.death_date.

conflicts.description: Hierarchical and directional concept links form N:M relationships not expressible in a flat entity.
conflicts.resolution: Retained concept_ancestor and concept_relationship as association/bridge resources.

conflicts.description: A person can have multiple overlapping payer plan periods (1:N), with no synthea counterpart.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved payer_plan_period as a 1:N child of person.

conflicts.description: Provider-to-facility is a many-to-one relationship; synthea names it 'organization' while OMOP names it 'care_site_id'.
conflicts.resolution: Unified both to care_site_id FK referencing care_site.

conflicts.description: OMOP explicitly declares primary keys; most synthea tables declare no primary key (only some, like patients.id, carry an id).
conflicts.resolution: Established explicit primary keys on all target resources, listing the corresponding synthea and OMOP source keys in source_provenance.

conflicts.description: synthea FK columns (patient, encounter, provider) are implicit and undeclared, while OMOP declares them via foreignKeys.
conflicts.resolution: Declared explicit foreign keys in the target (person_id, encounter_id, provider_id, care_site_id) and recorded the synthea and OMOP source columns in provenance.

conflicts.description: Several synthea event tables have no identifier column at all, preventing stable row identity.
conflicts.resolution: Introduced surrogate primary keys (condition_occurrence_id, observation_id, immunization_id, allergy_id, imaging_study_id) for these events.

conflicts.description: OMOP association tables rely on composite/natural keys rather than a single surrogate id.
conflicts.resolution: Modeled composite-key association resources as standalone tables without a single-column primary key.

conflicts.description: OMOP death shares its key with person (person_id) as a 1:1 extension.
conflicts.resolution: death.person_id modeled as both primary key and FK to person, with provenance listing both sources.
